Ethylene (C2H4)is a typical light hydrocarbon and essential building block. It has been reported that in 2021 the global requirement for C2H4was 220–230 million tons. There are also reports of the oxidative coupling of methane for C2H4production.[5] However, in addition to C2H4formation, the byproducts of acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2)are also generated.[6] Therefore, the selective removal of the two impurities C2H2and CO2is crucial for the recovery of polymer-grade C2H4from a ternary mixture of C2H2/CO2/C2H4because C2H2can poison the catalyst during C2H4polymerization while CO2reduces the

quality of the polyethylene (PE).[7] Current industrial separation technology mainly adopts multistep purification processes, including chemical adsorption of CO2(with associated huge solvent waste) and catalytic hydrogenation of C2H2(involving the use of noble-metal catalysts at high pressure/temperature),[8] wherein the energy consumption is huge.

Physical adsorption offers a potential solution for energyefficient separation.[9] It is noteworthy that although good separation of binary mixtures, including C2H2/C2H4[10]and C2H2/CO2[11]mixtures, is achieved by using adsorbents under ambient conditions, C2H4purification from CO2and C2H2contained in ternary mixtures presents a great challenge, as there is a lack of physisorbents that can selectively capture CO2/C2H2over C2H4. [12] A possible solution is the application of synergistic sorbent separation technology (SSST), by packing two or more physisorbents together.[13] Nevertheless, exploring the use of a single adsorbent that can exclude C2H4from a ternary mixture is considered most desirable. In addition, addressing the practical problem of determining the arrangement order and weight ratio of the corresponding adsorbents of the SSST also warrants attention.

Porous coordination polymers (PCPs), assembled from an organic linker and inorganic node, are a new type of crystalline material that exhibits significant ability to be tuned in nanopore chemistry for gas separation applications.[9b,14] Generally, in a sieving mechanism, the focus is on the use of differences

[Figure: Scheme 1. Schematic of the trap-and-flow channel crystal that allows shape- and size-dependent kinetic sieving and molecular trapping for highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture.]

in gas sizes, found in rigid PCPs with narrow apertures—only the molecule with the smaller size is adsorbed, while the molecule with the larger size is excluded.[9c,15] But the competitive host–guest interactions of two or more impurities in such a fitted porous system confound the adsorption equilibrium, especially in a tandem 1D channel. PCPs with framework dynamics are regarded as another platform for multicomponent separation because the corresponding response can enable the material to distinguish small differences within the multicomponent,[16] but the external conditions need to be accurately controlled (e.g., specific temperature, pressure, and gas ratio), and further coadsorption may occur once the pore is opened. Kinetic-dependent molecular diffusion has also been proposed for gas separation by creating sites of local motion in the crystal.[17] However, when the number of components in the gas mixture increases to three or more, special recognition devices are required in the channels.

In this work, we installed a three-bladed trap-and-flow channel in a crystal and were then subsequently able to achieve highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture that contained CO2and C2H2, even in the presence of moisture, and at a high temperature and wide gas ratio (Scheme 1). The flow channel featuring an optimized window aperture can kinetically distinguish between linear molecules of CO2or C2H2and a butterflylike molecule of C2H4while the trap in another channel allows the efficient capture of adsorbed molecules, as was determined computationally and observed experimentally at molecular level. In addition, the crystal synthesis in boiling alkaline solution offered excellent robustness under hot acid/base conditions.

2. Results and Discussion

2.1. Synthesis and Structural Characterization

The crystal transformation of NTU-65 in alkaline aqueous solution at 100°Cafforded a polyhedral-shaped crystal (NTU-67) (Figure S1, Supporting Information). This is mainly based on the consideration that crystal conversion in an aqueous solution may tailor nanopore in light of the size of the water template and inherit functional sites to a greater extent. Crystal transformation in alkaline aqueous may also reduce the energy state of the generated framework, realizing the assembly of chemically robust structure.[18] Direct synthesis of NTU-67 has also been attempted by tuning conditions and other solvent-triggered crystal conversions, but these attempts were unsuccessful.

Crystal analysis revealed that NTU-67 crystallizes in the space group of R32, where the asymmetric unit includes onehalf Cu2+cation, one-half SiF62-anion, and one L1 ligand, thus giving the same formula (MATH)·xSolvent) with that of NTU-65 (Table S1 and Figure S4, Supporting Information). In NTU-67, each ligand and SiF62-anion was connected by two Cu atoms, respectively, and each Cu2+cation was bridged by two F atoms from two SiF62-ions and four imidazoles (IM) N atoms from four ligands. The two F atoms in the para position of the SiF62-ion join the octahedral coordination of the two adjacent Cu2+cations to establish an inorganic helical chain along the axis. Therefore, the self-catenated square grid sheets formed between Cu2+cations and organic linkers are further connected by this chain to establish a three-dimensional (3D) framework (Figure S5, Supporting Information). Further topology analysis revealed that NTU-67 features a mmo net after subsuming the doubly connected ligands and SiF62-ions into the sixfold-connected Cu nodes, forming a new group of porous isomers with NTU-65 (pcu) (Figure 1a,b; Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information). Interestingly, two face-shared triangular channels (A and B) were observed in this new framework. Channel B with the narrowest hole of 3.4 Acan be considered a nanochannel for diffusion-promoted kinetic selectivities of CO2/C2H4and C2H2/C2H4. The limited space (MATH)that is regulated by three SiF62-anions and six IMs in Channel A can be regarded as a molecular trap for preferred adsorption. In addition, the arrangement of the molecular trap and nanochannel is trifoliate and interconnected (Figure  1c–j; Figures  S8 and  S9, Supporting Information). Calculated by Platon, the ideal porosity of NTU-67 is 28.4%. The structures and phase purities of the as-synthesized and activated NTU-67 were confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis and Le-Bail analysis (Figures  S10 and S11, Supporting Information). The thermogravimetric analysis collected from 25°Cto 300°Cshowed that the structure of NTU-67 was thermally stable up to 250°C, confirmed by variable temperature PXRD (Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information).

2.5. Crystallographic Study under Mixture

To explore the competitive binding of the gases, we analyzed the crystal structure of NTU-67 exposed to CO2/C2H4(2/8, v/v, 1 bar, 298 K). Of note here is that a mixture of C2H2/C2H4cannot be distinguished by X-ray diffraction measurement. Interestingly, one CO2molecule that interacts with F atoms was found in the molecular trap of channel A, while a unique onedimensional (1D) array of CO2and C2H4was found in channels B (Figure 4). This observation offers support that CO2is more preferentially adsorbed by the molecular trap, even under relative low partial pressure. In addition, 1D molecular array confirms that channel B provides an effective flow channel. This is a rare observation of competitive binding of the gases by a molecule-level crystallographic study.

2.6. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Aperture of Channels A and B

To determine the origin of the effective molecular sieving for a gas mixture through NTU-67, we performed ab initio

calculations for the size function (where the vdW radius is defined by the electronic density: isovalue 0.002). The molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4are given in Figure 5a–c. The largest pore size (indicated by the red ball in channel A (Figure  5d,e) is only 0.92 Å, which is much smaller than the molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4. Thus, all of these three gases can hardly pass through channel A. This result agrees well with the existence of a separated and isolated space in channel A (Figure 1d). The effective pore size of channel B was estimated on the three different cross sections, namely the center cross-section, the entrance cross-section, and the lower cross-section (Figure 5f–i). The red balls in Figure 5g–i express the vdW radius of a C atom (≈ 1.7 Å )for comparison. A comparison of Figure 5g,h indicates that there is a bottleneck going through channel B; there is a hole at the entrance cross-section of ≈ 3 . 4 Åin size. CO2and C2H2, with molecular sizes 3.40 and 3.68 Å, respectively, can pass through channel B, taking into account fluctuation and deformation of the channel structure. The hole size can be even larger than the molecular size of C2H2, depending on a time-dependent instantaneous channel structure. This means that structural modulation and deformation of the channel structure can play a critical role in molecular flow in NTU-67. In contrast, due to the restricted space, C2H4(molecular size 4.30 Å) passes through channel B with much more difficulty than CO2and C2H2.

Of even greater importance is the following. To pass through channel B, linear molecules such as C2H2and CO2should be aligned in wavy lines, as indicated in Figure  5j. 2.7. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Molecular Trap

To support the molecular trap scenario discussed above, we performed ab initio calculations for the adsorption energy of C2H2and C2H4. The numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H4and channel B·C2H4are higher than the numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H2and channel B·C2H2, respectively (Figures S36–S38, Supporting Information). We note that the computationally obtained bond distance is shorter than the experimentally observed bond distance, as the former corresponds to the minimum energy structure calculated at 0Kwhile the latter includes thermal fluctuation and structural disorder at 298 K. We then selected three SiF62-ions and a gas molecule to calculate the adsorption energy because SiF62-ions are the most important and essential adsorption sites (Figures  S40 and S41, Supporting Information). The resulting adsorption energy of C2H2is higher than that of C2H4(in channel A 1.5 times and in channel B 1.25 times). The C2H2-involved bond distance is shorter than the C2H4-involved bond distance, in both channels A and B. The shorter distance

overcomes the order of the numbers of bonds and makes the adsorption energy of C2H2higher than the adsorption energy of C2H4. The faster flow and the higher adsorption energy enable C2H2to locate molecular traps existing in channel A more effectively than C2H4, leading to the sieving separation of C2H4from a C2H2/C2H4mixture. These computational insights are in good agreement with the experimental observations of the isosteric enthalpy and the gas-loaded crystal analysis, as well as with the higher adsorption rates of C2H2compared with C2H4as seen in Figures 2–4.

2.8. Improved Kinetic Selectivity Achieved with a Three-Bladed Array

To validate the collaborative roles of the nanospace, the adsorption kinetics of each gas were evaluated on NTU-67 at 298 K (Figure 6; Figures S42 and S43, Supporting Information). The pressure change indicates that the adsorption rate of CO2is much higher than that of C2H4. The kinetic selectivity of CO2/C2H4is 5.26, while that of C2H2/C2H4is 3.86. For comparison, adsorption kinetics of the gases were also collected in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the framework with the same SiF62-ion and a square window aperture. The kinetic selectivities of both CO2/C2H4(3.50) and C2H2/C2H4(2.49) in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i are lower than on NTU-67. The advantages of NTU-67 can be rationalized by the enhanced CO2and C2H2diffusion and molecular trapping by the three-bladed array. As computationally indicated above, the nanochannel allows CO2and C2H2to smoothly flow along channel B, while the molecular trap provides effective trapping sites for them, resulting in the current dynamic sieving in NTU-67. In contrast, because adsorption sites and flow paths exist in the same 1D channel in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the adsorbed molecules occupy the limited space in the 1D channel, making it difficult for subsequent molecules to pass through.

2.9. Molecular Trapping Effect

Based on the different trap–guest interactions and size effect, as well as the computational insights supporting them, the effect of molecular trapping was explored under dynamic conditions. Sequential controlled blowing tests on NTU-67 were carried out. At 298 K, adsorption-saturated NTU-67 with C2H2/CO2mixtures (NTU-67@C2H2·CO2)was swept by He flow to remove the loosely adsorbed components. Effluents of

C2H2and CO2were detected after heating the system to 393K(Figure 7a). Negligible amounts of C2H2and CO2were eluted from the bed after changing the sweeping gas of He to C2H4(Figure 7b). Further He sweeping was performed until no more gas was detected. C2H2and CO2, but no C2H4, were detected in the final heating stage, thus confirming the preferred selection of C2H2and CO2compared with C2H4by the molecular trap in NTU-67. In fact, only a small amount of adsorbed C2H4was adsorbed in NTU-67@C2H4that can also be replaced by the C2H2/CO2mixture (Figure 7c,d).

2.10. Breakthrough Separations

Encouraged by the functions of the trap-and-flow channel, the separation ability of NTU-67 to gas mixture was evaluated by breakthrough experiments. With the feed gas of C2H2/C2H4mixtures (MATH), 1/99, v/v), polymer-grade C2 H4 (> 99.95%)elutes out at 8.1 min, while C2H2was captured before the breakpoint at 41.4  min (Figure 8a). When the gas feed changed to CO2/C2H4(5 mL min−1 , 50/50, v/v) (Figure 8b), pure C2H4was also detected at first, while, CO2was absorbed. The retention time for CO2was 37.4 min, confirming the outstanding ability for selective CO2capture from CO2/C2H4mixtures.

In light of these outstanding performances, we next conducted separation experiments with ternary feed gas of C2H2/CO2/C2H4/5 m L m i n-1, 1/9/90, v/v/v, 1 bar), a general industrial mixture from oxidative coupling of methane.[6a] Likewise, NTU-67 selectively captured C2H2and CO2simultaneously, and yielded C2H4(> 99.95%)within 27.0 minin the column outlet at 298 K (Figure 8c). 2.11. Stability Evaluation

The adsorbent should own good water stability, which is necessary for practical application.[22] Due to the alkaline solutioninduced crystal conversion, the stability of NTU-67 is strongly expected. After treating the crystals in an acid-based solution (MATH), 7, and 12) at 373 K for 4 days or at 298 K for 120 days, respectively, the crystallinity, morphology, pore volume, and pore size distribution of NTU-67 were analyzed (Figure 9a, Figure S71–S73 and Table S4, Supporting Information). From the PXRD, nearly all peak positions are same with the as-synthesized phase. Meanwhile, we also note the intensity change of some peaks, such as the peak at 13.3°and 24.7°for the samples of NTU-67 (MATH), 373 K, 4 days and pH = 12, 373 K, 4 days). This may be due to the partial change of the exposed crystal plane during high-temperature treatment. In addition, CO2uptakes and pore size distribution of the treated samples are slightly higher or larger than that of the as-synthesized phase, as the generated tiny cracks of the treated crystals, validated by SEM images. In contrast, SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni totally lost their crystallinity after chemical treatment, while UTSA-300 dissolved in all solution immediately at room temperature (Figure S74, Supporting Information). Moreover, after all breakthrough experiments, the NTU-67 also keeps the same diffraction with original peaks. In light of these, a breakthrough experiment of CO2/C2H2/C2H4(1/9/90, v/v/v)with water vapor (relative humidity: 22%) was also conducted. The breakpoints of C2H4and C2H2were same as for the curves with dry feed gas, however, the breakpoint of CO2becomes a little earlier when compared with that of the measurement under dry gas. Further cycle measurements under moisture reveal that same curves were observed, despite it has vapor uptake (Figure  9b and Figure S76, Supporting Information). Keeping the structures and preparation method in mind, this excellent stability should be assigned as a reduction in the framework energy

3. Conclusion

Adsorption-based gas purification from multicomponent mixtures offers a very good opportunity to replace the conventional energy-consuming separation process, the requirements being a porous material having integrated properties of simultaneous adsorption selectivity toward one component, high capacity, and excellent stability. Using the post-synthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution, we achieved these required factors in NTU-67, a new trapand-flow crystal. Crystallographic studies under pure gas and mixed gases validate the positive effect of the molecular trap for C2H2and CO2capture. Further Ab calculations and blowing tests reveal that linear molecules of C2H2and CO2diffuse much faster than the butterfly-like C2H4in flow channel B. In addition, the interchannel window between channels A and B allows the gas to flow into the molecular trap existing in channel A. More interestingly, the three-bladed array of the trap and flow channels promotes the crystal to afford increased kinetic selectivity. This unique and promising architecture allows highly efficient polymer-grade C2H4purification from C2H2/CO2/C2H4mixtures under dynamic condition, even in the presence of moisture, at high temperature and with a wide gas ratio. Meanwhile, it is worthy to note that the robustness of the NTU-67 framework reflects that crystal conversion in hot water or chemical solution is a good choice to establish stable PCPs. Therefore, our findings, specifically, the record C2H4productivity achieved here, coupled with molecular-level insight gained into the trap-and-flow channels, offer an innovative route for the design of advanced physisorbents for further challenging separations.

Shape- and Size-Dependent Kinetic Ethylene Sieving from a Ternary Mixture by a Trap-and-Flow Channel Crystal

Qiubing Dong, Yuhang Huang, Kim Hyeon-Deuk, I-Ya Chang, Jingmeng Wan, Changlin Chen, Jingui Duan,* Wanqin Jin, and Susumu Kitagawa*

Ethylene (C2H4)purification from multicomponent mixtures by physical adsorption presents a great challenge in the chemical industry. This work successfully uses the postsynthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution to synthesize a trap-and-flow channel crystal (namely NTU-67), the flow channel of which provides an effective shape- and sizedependent sieving path for linear molecules such as acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2), while the adjacent channel possesses customized space for efficient molecular trapping. The three-bladed array of the nanospace enables the crystal to afford a record productivity of C2H4(121.5 mL g−1 , (MATH)from 22/2/24(7/9/90, v/v/v)mixtures in a single adsorption–desorption cycle under humid and dynamic conditions, even at a high temperature of 343 K and wide gas ratio. The molecular-level insight and mechanism of the cooperative role of the trap-and-flow channel, found computationally and observed experimentally, demonstrates a new design philosophy toward extending the application boundaries of porous coordination polymers to further challenging tasks.

1. Introduction

Separations by porous materials is a crucial process in our daily lives as well as in industry.[1] For example, zeolite adsorbents in respirators can increase the oxygen concentration to meet medical standards,[2] while activated carbons are used as typical adsorbents for water purification.[3] However, a most challenging process in industry is the separation of light

Ethylene (C2H4)is a typical light hydrocarbon and essential building block. It has been reported that in 2021 the global requirement for C2H4was 220–230 million tons. There are also reports of the oxidative coupling of methane for C2H4production.[5] However, in addition to C2H4formation, the byproducts of acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2)are also generated.[6] Therefore, the selective removal of the two impurities C2H2and CO2is crucial for the recovery of polymer-grade C2H4from a ternary mixture of C2H2/CO2/C2H4because C2H2can poison the catalyst during C2H4polymerization while CO2reduces the

quality of the polyethylene (PE).[7] Current industrial separation technology mainly adopts multistep purification processes, including chemical adsorption of CO2(with associated huge solvent waste) and catalytic hydrogenation of C2H2(involving the use of noble-metal catalysts at high pressure/temperature),[8] wherein the energy consumption is huge.

Physical adsorption offers a potential solution for energyefficient separation.[9] It is noteworthy that although good separation of binary mixtures, including C2H2/C2H4[10]and C2H2/CO2[11]mixtures, is achieved by using adsorbents under ambient conditions, C2H4purification from CO2and C2H2contained in ternary mixtures presents a great challenge, as there is a lack of physisorbents that can selectively capture CO2/C2H2over C2H4. [12] A possible solution is the application of synergistic sorbent separation technology (SSST), by packing two or more physisorbents together.[13] Nevertheless, exploring the use of a single adsorbent that can exclude C2H4from a ternary mixture is considered most desirable. In addition, addressing the practical problem of determining the arrangement order and weight ratio of the corresponding adsorbents of the SSST also warrants attention.

Porous coordination polymers (PCPs), assembled from an organic linker and inorganic node, are a new type of crystalline material that exhibits significant ability to be tuned in nanopore chemistry for gas separation applications.[9b,14] Generally, in a sieving mechanism, the focus is on the use of differences

[Figure: Scheme 1. Schematic of the trap-and-flow channel crystal that allows shape- and size-dependent kinetic sieving and molecular trapping for highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture.]

in gas sizes, found in rigid PCPs with narrow apertures—only the molecule with the smaller size is adsorbed, while the molecule with the larger size is excluded.[9c,15] But the competitive host–guest interactions of two or more impurities in such a fitted porous system confound the adsorption equilibrium, especially in a tandem 1D channel. PCPs with framework dynamics are regarded as another platform for multicomponent separation because the corresponding response can enable the material to distinguish small differences within the multicomponent,[16] but the external conditions need to be accurately controlled (e.g., specific temperature, pressure, and gas ratio), and further coadsorption may occur once the pore is opened. Kinetic-dependent molecular diffusion has also been proposed for gas separation by creating sites of local motion in the crystal.[17] However, when the number of components in the gas mixture increases to three or more, special recognition devices are required in the channels.

In this work, we installed a three-bladed trap-and-flow channel in a crystal and were then subsequently able to achieve highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture that contained CO2and C2H2, even in the presence of moisture, and at a high temperature and wide gas ratio (Scheme 1). The flow channel featuring an optimized window aperture can kinetically distinguish between linear molecules of CO2or C2H2and a butterflylike molecule of C2H4while the trap in another channel allows the efficient capture of adsorbed molecules, as was determined computationally and observed experimentally at molecular level. In addition, the crystal synthesis in boiling alkaline solution offered excellent robustness under hot acid/base conditions.

2. Results and Discussion

2.1. Synthesis and Structural Characterization

The crystal transformation of NTU-65 in alkaline aqueous solution at 100°Cafforded a polyhedral-shaped crystal (NTU-67) (Figure S1, Supporting Information). This is mainly based on the consideration that crystal conversion in an aqueous solution may tailor nanopore in light of the size of the water template and inherit functional sites to a greater extent. Crystal transformation in alkaline aqueous may also reduce the energy state of the generated framework, realizing the assembly of chemically robust structure.[18] Direct synthesis of NTU-67 has also been attempted by tuning conditions and other solvent-triggered crystal conversions, but these attempts were unsuccessful.

Crystal analysis revealed that NTU-67 crystallizes in the space group of R32, where the asymmetric unit includes onehalf Cu2+cation, one-half SiF62-anion, and one L1 ligand, thus giving the same formula (MATH)·xSolvent) with that of NTU-65 (Table S1 and Figure S4, Supporting Information). In NTU-67, each ligand and SiF62-anion was connected by two Cu atoms, respectively, and each Cu2+cation was bridged by two F atoms from two SiF62-ions and four imidazoles (IM) N atoms from four ligands. The two F atoms in the para position of the SiF62-ion join the octahedral coordination of the two adjacent Cu2+cations to establish an inorganic helical chain along the axis. Therefore, the self-catenated square grid sheets formed between Cu2+cations and organic linkers are further connected by this chain to establish a three-dimensional (3D) framework (Figure S5, Supporting Information). Further topology analysis revealed that NTU-67 features a mmo net after subsuming the doubly connected ligands and SiF62-ions into the sixfold-connected Cu nodes, forming a new group of porous isomers with NTU-65 (pcu) (Figure 1a,b; Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information). Interestingly, two face-shared triangular channels (A and B) were observed in this new framework. Channel B with the narrowest hole of 3.4 Acan be considered a nanochannel for diffusion-promoted kinetic selectivities of CO2/C2H4and C2H2/C2H4. The limited space (MATH)that is regulated by three SiF62-anions and six IMs in Channel A can be regarded as a molecular trap for preferred adsorption. In addition, the arrangement of the molecular trap and nanochannel is trifoliate and interconnected (Figure  1c–j; Figures  S8 and  S9, Supporting Information). Calculated by Platon, the ideal porosity of NTU-67 is 28.4%. The structures and phase purities of the as-synthesized and activated NTU-67 were confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis and Le-Bail analysis (Figures  S10 and S11, Supporting Information). The thermogravimetric analysis collected from 25°Cto 300°Cshowed that the structure of NTU-67 was thermally stable up to 250°C, confirmed by variable temperature PXRD (Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information).

2.5. Crystallographic Study under Mixture

To explore the competitive binding of the gases, we analyzed the crystal structure of NTU-67 exposed to CO2/C2H4(2/8, v/v, 1 bar, 298 K). Of note here is that a mixture of C2H2/C2H4cannot be distinguished by X-ray diffraction measurement. Interestingly, one CO2molecule that interacts with F atoms was found in the molecular trap of channel A, while a unique onedimensional (1D) array of CO2and C2H4was found in channels B (Figure 4). This observation offers support that CO2is more preferentially adsorbed by the molecular trap, even under relative low partial pressure. In addition, 1D molecular array confirms that channel B provides an effective flow channel. This is a rare observation of competitive binding of the gases by a molecule-level crystallographic study.

2.6. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Aperture of Channels A and B

To determine the origin of the effective molecular sieving for a gas mixture through NTU-67, we performed ab initio

calculations for the size function (where the vdW radius is defined by the electronic density: isovalue 0.002). The molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4are given in Figure 5a–c. The largest pore size (indicated by the red ball in channel A (Figure  5d,e) is only 0.92 Å, which is much smaller than the molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4. Thus, all of these three gases can hardly pass through channel A. This result agrees well with the existence of a separated and isolated space in channel A (Figure 1d). The effective pore size of channel B was estimated on the three different cross sections, namely the center cross-section, the entrance cross-section, and the lower cross-section (Figure 5f–i). The red balls in Figure 5g–i express the vdW radius of a C atom (≈ 1.7 Å )for comparison. A comparison of Figure 5g,h indicates that there is a bottleneck going through channel B; there is a hole at the entrance cross-section of ≈ 3 . 4 Åin size. CO2and C2H2, with molecular sizes 3.40 and 3.68 Å, respectively, can pass through channel B, taking into account fluctuation and deformation of the channel structure. The hole size can be even larger than the molecular size of C2H2, depending on a time-dependent instantaneous channel structure. This means that structural modulation and deformation of the channel structure can play a critical role in molecular flow in NTU-67. In contrast, due to the restricted space, C2H4(molecular size 4.30 Å) passes through channel B with much more difficulty than CO2and C2H2.

Of even greater importance is the following. To pass through channel B, linear molecules such as C2H2and CO2should be aligned in wavy lines, as indicated in Figure  5j. In channel B, linear molecules can pass through only the channel indicated with a red arrow, along which the passable holes of ≈ 3.4 Åexist. Such wavy nanochannels coincide with the 1D molecular array observed in Figure  4b. Because the energetically most stable adsorbed structure of C2H2does not form the wavy line, but rather leads to the zigzag adsorbed structure in channel B (Figures S38 and S39, Supporting Information), the actual adsorption structure of C2H2is determined not only energetically but also dynamically; duplicating upside down the most stable adsorbed structure achieved in the unit cell leads to the zigzag adsorbed structure in channel B. 2.7. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Molecular Trap

To support the molecular trap scenario discussed above, we performed ab initio calculations for the adsorption energy of C2H2and C2H4. The numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H4and channel B·C2H4are higher than the numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H2and channel B·C2H2, respectively (Figures S36–S38, Supporting Information). We note that the computationally obtained bond distance is shorter than the experimentally observed bond distance, as the former corresponds to the minimum energy structure calculated at 0Kwhile the latter includes thermal fluctuation and structural disorder at 298 K. We then selected three SiF62-ions and a gas molecule to calculate the adsorption energy because SiF62-ions are the most important and essential adsorption sites (Figures  S40 and S41, Supporting Information). The resulting adsorption energy of C2H2is higher than that of C2H4(in channel A 1.5 times and in channel B 1.25 times). The C2H2-involved bond distance is shorter than the C2H4-involved bond distance, in both channels A and B. The shorter distance

overcomes the order of the numbers of bonds and makes the adsorption energy of C2H2higher than the adsorption energy of C2H4. The faster flow and the higher adsorption energy enable C2H2to locate molecular traps existing in channel A more effectively than C2H4, leading to the sieving separation of C2H4from a C2H2/C2H4mixture. These computational insights are in good agreement with the experimental observations of the isosteric enthalpy and the gas-loaded crystal analysis, as well as with the higher adsorption rates of C2H2compared with C2H4as seen in Figures 2–4.

2.8. Improved Kinetic Selectivity Achieved with a Three-Bladed Array

To validate the collaborative roles of the nanospace, the adsorption kinetics of each gas were evaluated on NTU-67 at 298 K (Figure 6; Figures S42 and S43, Supporting Information). The pressure change indicates that the adsorption rate of CO2is much higher than that of C2H4. The kinetic selectivity of CO2/C2H4is 5.26, while that of C2H2/C2H4is 3.86. For comparison, adsorption kinetics of the gases were also collected in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the framework with the same SiF62-ion and a square window aperture. The kinetic selectivities of both CO2/C2H4(3.50) and C2H2/C2H4(2.49) in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i are lower than on NTU-67. The advantages of NTU-67 can be rationalized by the enhanced CO2and C2H2diffusion and molecular trapping by the three-bladed array. As computationally indicated above, the nanochannel allows CO2and C2H2to smoothly flow along channel B, while the molecular trap provides effective trapping sites for them, resulting in the current dynamic sieving in NTU-67. In contrast, because adsorption sites and flow paths exist in the same 1D channel in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the adsorbed molecules occupy the limited space in the 1D channel, making it difficult for subsequent molecules to pass through.

2.9. Molecular Trapping Effect

Based on the different trap–guest interactions and size effect, as well as the computational insights supporting them, the effect of molecular trapping was explored under dynamic conditions. Sequential controlled blowing tests on NTU-67 were carried out. At 298 K, adsorption-saturated NTU-67 with C2H2/CO2mixtures (NTU-67@C2H2·CO2)was swept by He flow to remove the loosely adsorbed components. Effluents of

C2H2and CO2were detected after heating the system to 393K(Figure 7a). Negligible amounts of C2H2and CO2were eluted from the bed after changing the sweeping gas of He to C2H4(Figure 7b). Further He sweeping was performed until no more gas was detected. C2H2and CO2, but no C2H4, were detected in the final heating stage, thus confirming the preferred selection of C2H2and CO2compared with C2H4by the molecular trap in NTU-67. In fact, only a small amount of adsorbed C2H4was adsorbed in NTU-67@C2H4that can also be replaced by the C2H2/CO2mixture (Figure 7c,d).

2.11. Stability Evaluation

The adsorbent should own good water stability, which is necessary for practical application.[22] Due to the alkaline solutioninduced crystal conversion, the stability of NTU-67 is strongly expected. After treating the crystals in an acid-based solution (MATH), 7, and 12) at 373 K for 4 days or at 298 K for 120 days, respectively, the crystallinity, morphology, pore volume, and pore size distribution of NTU-67 were analyzed (Figure 9a, Figure S71–S73 and Table S4, Supporting Information). From the PXRD, nearly all peak positions are same with the as-synthesized phase. Meanwhile, we also note the intensity change of some peaks, such as the peak at 13.3°and 24.7°for the samples of NTU-67 (MATH), 373 K, 4 days and pH = 12, 373 K, 4 days). This may be due to the partial change of the exposed crystal plane during high-temperature treatment. In addition, CO2uptakes and pore size distribution of the treated samples are slightly higher or larger than that of the as-synthesized phase, as the generated tiny cracks of the treated crystals, validated by SEM images. In contrast, SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni totally lost their crystallinity after chemical treatment, while UTSA-300 dissolved in all solution immediately at room temperature (Figure S74, Supporting Information). Moreover, after all breakthrough experiments, the NTU-67 also keeps the same diffraction with original peaks. In light of these, a breakthrough experiment of CO2/C2H2/C2H4(1/9/90, v/v/v)with water vapor (relative humidity: 22%) was also conducted. The breakpoints of C2H4and C2H2were same as for the curves with dry feed gas, however, the breakpoint of CO2becomes a little earlier when compared with that of the measurement under dry gas. Further cycle measurements under moisture reveal that same curves were observed, despite it has vapor uptake (Figure  9b and Figure S76, Supporting Information). Keeping the structures and preparation method in mind, this excellent stability should be assigned as a reduction in the framework energy

3. Conclusion

Adsorption-based gas purification from multicomponent mixtures offers a very good opportunity to replace the conventional energy-consuming separation process, the requirements being a porous material having integrated properties of simultaneous adsorption selectivity toward one component, high capacity, and excellent stability. Using the post-synthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution, we achieved these required factors in NTU-67, a new trapand-flow crystal. Crystallographic studies under pure gas and mixed gases validate the positive effect of the molecular trap for C2H2and CO2capture. Further Ab calculations and blowing tests reveal that linear molecules of C2H2and CO2diffuse much faster than the butterfly-like C2H4in flow channel B. In addition, the interchannel window between channels A and B allows the gas to flow into the molecular trap existing in channel A. More interestingly, the three-bladed array of the trap and flow channels promotes the crystal to afford increased kinetic selectivity. This unique and promising architecture allows highly efficient polymer-grade C2H4purification from C2H2/CO2/C2H4mixtures under dynamic condition, even in the presence of moisture, at high temperature and with a wide gas ratio. Meanwhile, it is worthy to note that the robustness of the NTU-67 framework reflects that crystal conversion in hot water or chemical solution is a good choice to establish stable PCPs. Therefore, our findings, specifically, the record C2H4productivity achieved here, coupled with molecular-level insight gained into the trap-and-flow channels, offer an innovative route for the design of advanced physisorbents for further challenging separations.

Shape- and Size-Dependent Kinetic Ethylene Sieving from a Ternary Mixture by a Trap-and-Flow Channel Crystal

Qiubing Dong, Yuhang Huang, Kim Hyeon-Deuk, I-Ya Chang, Jingmeng Wan, Changlin Chen, Jingui Duan,* Wanqin Jin, and Susumu Kitagawa*

Ethylene (C2H4)purification from multicomponent mixtures by physical adsorption presents a great challenge in the chemical industry. This work successfully uses the postsynthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution to synthesize a trap-and-flow channel crystal (namely NTU-67), the flow channel of which provides an effective shape- and sizedependent sieving path for linear molecules such as acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2), while the adjacent channel possesses customized space for efficient molecular trapping. The three-bladed array of the nanospace enables the crystal to afford a record productivity of C2H4(121.5 mL g−1 , (MATH)from 22/2/24(7/9/90, v/v/v)mixtures in a single adsorption–desorption cycle under humid and dynamic conditions, even at a high temperature of 343 K and wide gas ratio. The molecular-level insight and mechanism of the cooperative role of the trap-and-flow channel, found computationally and observed experimentally, demonstrates a new design philosophy toward extending the application boundaries of porous coordination polymers to further challenging tasks.

1. Introduction

Separations by porous materials is a crucial process in our daily lives as well as in industry.[1] For example, zeolite adsorbents in respirators can increase the oxygen concentration to meet medical standards,[2] while activated carbons are used as typical adsorbents for water purification.[3] However, a most challenging process in industry is the separation of light

hydrocarbons, due to their very similar sizes and volatilities. Therefore, the establishment and development of advanced porous adsorbents for this challenging task are urgently required, with preferably broad application prospects, in terms of high efficiency and energy savings.[4]

Ethylene (C2H4)is a typical light hydrocarbon and essential building block. It has been reported that in 2021 the global requirement for C2H4was 220–230 million tons. There are also reports of the oxidative coupling of methane for C2H4production.[5] However, in addition to C2H4formation, the byproducts of acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2)are also generated.[6] Therefore, the selective removal of the two impurities C2H2and CO2is crucial for the recovery of polymer-grade C2H4from a ternary mixture of C2H2/CO2/C2H4because C2H2can poison the catalyst during C2H4polymerization while CO2reduces the

quality of the polyethylene (PE).[7] Current industrial separation technology mainly adopts multistep purification processes, including chemical adsorption of CO2(with associated huge solvent waste) and catalytic hydrogenation of C2H2(involving the use of noble-metal catalysts at high pressure/temperature),[8] wherein the energy consumption is huge.

Physical adsorption offers a potential solution for energyefficient separation.[9] It is noteworthy that although good separation of binary mixtures, including C2H2/C2H4[10]and C2H2/CO2[11]mixtures, is achieved by using adsorbents under ambient conditions, C2H4purification from CO2and C2H2contained in ternary mixtures presents a great challenge, as there is a lack of physisorbents that can selectively capture CO2/C2H2over C2H4. [12] A possible solution is the application of synergistic sorbent separation technology (SSST), by packing two or more physisorbents together.[13] Nevertheless, exploring the use of a single adsorbent that can exclude C2H4from a ternary mixture is considered most desirable. In addition, addressing the practical problem of determining the arrangement order and weight ratio of the corresponding adsorbents of the SSST also warrants attention.

Porous coordination polymers (PCPs), assembled from an organic linker and inorganic node, are a new type of crystalline material that exhibits significant ability to be tuned in nanopore chemistry for gas separation applications.[9b,14] Generally, in a sieving mechanism, the focus is on the use of differences

[Figure: Scheme 1. Schematic of the trap-and-flow channel crystal that allows shape- and size-dependent kinetic sieving and molecular trapping for highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture.]

in gas sizes, found in rigid PCPs with narrow apertures—only the molecule with the smaller size is adsorbed, while the molecule with the larger size is excluded.[9c,15] But the competitive host–guest interactions of two or more impurities in such a fitted porous system confound the adsorption equilibrium, especially in a tandem 1D channel. PCPs with framework dynamics are regarded as another platform for multicomponent separation because the corresponding response can enable the material to distinguish small differences within the multicomponent,[16] but the external conditions need to be accurately controlled (e.g., specific temperature, pressure, and gas ratio), and further coadsorption may occur once the pore is opened. Kinetic-dependent molecular diffusion has also been proposed for gas separation by creating sites of local motion in the crystal.[17] However, when the number of components in the gas mixture increases to three or more, special recognition devices are required in the channels.

In this work, we installed a three-bladed trap-and-flow channel in a crystal and were then subsequently able to achieve highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture that contained CO2and C2H2, even in the presence of moisture, and at a high temperature and wide gas ratio (Scheme 1). The flow channel featuring an optimized window aperture can kinetically distinguish between linear molecules of CO2or C2H2and a butterflylike molecule of C2H4while the trap in another channel allows the efficient capture of adsorbed molecules, as was determined computationally and observed experimentally at molecular level. In addition, the crystal synthesis in boiling alkaline solution offered excellent robustness under hot acid/base conditions.

2. Results and Discussion

2.1. Synthesis and Structural Characterization

The crystal transformation of NTU-65 in alkaline aqueous solution at 100°Cafforded a polyhedral-shaped crystal (NTU-67) (Figure S1, Supporting Information). This is mainly based on the consideration that crystal conversion in an aqueous solution may tailor nanopore in light of the size of the water template and inherit functional sites to a greater extent. Crystal transformation in alkaline aqueous may also reduce the energy state of the generated framework, realizing the assembly of chemically robust structure.[18] Direct synthesis of NTU-67 has also been attempted by tuning conditions and other solvent-triggered crystal conversions, but these attempts were unsuccessful.

Crystal analysis revealed that NTU-67 crystallizes in the space group of R32, where the asymmetric unit includes onehalf Cu2+cation, one-half SiF62-anion, and one L1 ligand, thus giving the same formula (MATH)·xSolvent) with that of NTU-65 (Table S1 and Figure S4, Supporting Information). In NTU-67, each ligand and SiF62-anion was connected by two Cu atoms, respectively, and each Cu2+cation was bridged by two F atoms from two SiF62-ions and four imidazoles (IM) N atoms from four ligands. The two F atoms in the para position of the SiF62-ion join the octahedral coordination of the two adjacent Cu2+cations to establish an inorganic helical chain along the axis. Therefore, the self-catenated square grid sheets formed between Cu2+cations and organic linkers are further connected by this chain to establish a three-dimensional (3D) framework (Figure S5, Supporting Information). Further topology analysis revealed that NTU-67 features a mmo net after subsuming the doubly connected ligands and SiF62-ions into the sixfold-connected Cu nodes, forming a new group of porous isomers with NTU-65 (pcu) (Figure 1a,b; Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information). Interestingly, two face-shared triangular channels (A and B) were observed in this new framework. Channel B with the narrowest hole of 3.4 Acan be considered a nanochannel for diffusion-promoted kinetic selectivities of CO2/C2H4and C2H2/C2H4. The limited space (MATH)that is regulated by three SiF62-anions and six IMs in Channel A can be regarded as a molecular trap for preferred adsorption. In addition, the arrangement of the molecular trap and nanochannel is trifoliate and interconnected (Figure  1c–j; Figures  S8 and  S9, Supporting Information). Calculated by Platon, the ideal porosity of NTU-67 is 28.4%. The structures and phase purities of the as-synthesized and activated NTU-67 were confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis and Le-Bail analysis (Figures  S10 and S11, Supporting Information). The thermogravimetric analysis collected from 25°Cto 300°Cshowed that the structure of NTU-67 was thermally stable up to 250°C, confirmed by variable temperature PXRD (Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information).

2.5. Crystallographic Study under Mixture

To explore the competitive binding of the gases, we analyzed the crystal structure of NTU-67 exposed to CO2/C2H4(2/8, v/v, 1 bar, 298 K). Of note here is that a mixture of C2H2/C2H4cannot be distinguished by X-ray diffraction measurement. Interestingly, one CO2molecule that interacts with F atoms was found in the molecular trap of channel A, while a unique onedimensional (1D) array of CO2and C2H4was found in channels B (Figure 4). This observation offers support that CO2is more preferentially adsorbed by the molecular trap, even under relative low partial pressure. In addition, 1D molecular array confirms that channel B provides an effective flow channel. This is a rare observation of competitive binding of the gases by a molecule-level crystallographic study.

2.6. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Aperture of Channels A and B

To determine the origin of the effective molecular sieving for a gas mixture through NTU-67, we performed ab initio

calculations for the size function (where the vdW radius is defined by the electronic density: isovalue 0.002). The molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4are given in Figure 5a–c. The largest pore size (indicated by the red ball in channel A (Figure  5d,e) is only 0.92 Å, which is much smaller than the molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4. Thus, all of these three gases can hardly pass through channel A. This result agrees well with the existence of a separated and isolated space in channel A (Figure 1d). The effective pore size of channel B was estimated on the three different cross sections, namely the center cross-section, the entrance cross-section, and the lower cross-section (Figure 5f–i). The red balls in Figure 5g–i express the vdW radius of a C atom (≈ 1.7 Å )for comparison. A comparison of Figure 5g,h indicates that there is a bottleneck going through channel B; there is a hole at the entrance cross-section of ≈ 3 . 4 Åin size. CO2and C2H2, with molecular sizes 3.40 and 3.68 Å, respectively, can pass through channel B, taking into account fluctuation and deformation of the channel structure. The hole size can be even larger than the molecular size of C2H2, depending on a time-dependent instantaneous channel structure. This means that structural modulation and deformation of the channel structure can play a critical role in molecular flow in NTU-67. In contrast, due to the restricted space, C2H4(molecular size 4.30 Å) passes through channel B with much more difficulty than CO2and C2H2.

Of even greater importance is the following. To pass through channel B, linear molecules such as C2H2and CO2should be aligned in wavy lines, as indicated in Figure  5j. In channel B, linear molecules can pass through only the channel indicated with a red arrow, along which the passable holes of ≈ 3.4 Åexist. Such wavy nanochannels coincide with the 1D molecular array observed in Figure  4b. Because the energetically most stable adsorbed structure of C2H2does not form the wavy line, but rather leads to the zigzag adsorbed structure in channel B (Figures S38 and S39, Supporting Information), the actual adsorption structure of C2H2is determined not only energetically but also dynamically; duplicating upside down the most stable adsorbed structure achieved in the unit cell leads to the zigzag adsorbed structure in channel B. 2.7. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Molecular Trap

To support the molecular trap scenario discussed above, we performed ab initio calculations for the adsorption energy of C2H2and C2H4. The numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H4and channel B·C2H4are higher than the numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H2and channel B·C2H2, respectively (Figures S36–S38, Supporting Information). We note that the computationally obtained bond distance is shorter than the experimentally observed bond distance, as the former corresponds to the minimum energy structure calculated at 0Kwhile the latter includes thermal fluctuation and structural disorder at 298 K. We then selected three SiF62-ions and a gas molecule to calculate the adsorption energy because SiF62-ions are the most important and essential adsorption sites (Figures  S40 and S41, Supporting Information). The resulting adsorption energy of C2H2is higher than that of C2H4(in channel A 1.5 times and in channel B 1.25 times). The C2H2-involved bond distance is shorter than the C2H4-involved bond distance, in both channels A and B. The shorter distance

overcomes the order of the numbers of bonds and makes the adsorption energy of C2H2higher than the adsorption energy of C2H4. The faster flow and the higher adsorption energy enable C2H2to locate molecular traps existing in channel A more effectively than C2H4, leading to the sieving separation of C2H4from a C2H2/C2H4mixture. These computational insights are in good agreement with the experimental observations of the isosteric enthalpy and the gas-loaded crystal analysis, as well as with the higher adsorption rates of C2H2compared with C2H4as seen in Figures 2–4.

2.8. Improved Kinetic Selectivity Achieved with a Three-Bladed Array

To validate the collaborative roles of the nanospace, the adsorption kinetics of each gas were evaluated on NTU-67 at 298 K (Figure 6; Figures S42 and S43, Supporting Information). The pressure change indicates that the adsorption rate of CO2is much higher than that of C2H4. The kinetic selectivity of CO2/C2H4is 5.26, while that of C2H2/C2H4is 3.86. For comparison, adsorption kinetics of the gases were also collected in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the framework with the same SiF62-ion and a square window aperture. The kinetic selectivities of both CO2/C2H4(3.50) and C2H2/C2H4(2.49) in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i are lower than on NTU-67. The advantages of NTU-67 can be rationalized by the enhanced CO2and C2H2diffusion and molecular trapping by the three-bladed array. As computationally indicated above, the nanochannel allows CO2and C2H2to smoothly flow along channel B, while the molecular trap provides effective trapping sites for them, resulting in the current dynamic sieving in NTU-67. In contrast, because adsorption sites and flow paths exist in the same 1D channel in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the adsorbed molecules occupy the limited space in the 1D channel, making it difficult for subsequent molecules to pass through.

2.9. Molecular Trapping Effect

Based on the different trap–guest interactions and size effect, as well as the computational insights supporting them, the effect of molecular trapping was explored under dynamic conditions. Sequential controlled blowing tests on NTU-67 were carried out. At 298 K, adsorption-saturated NTU-67 with C2H2/CO2mixtures (NTU-67@C2H2·CO2)was swept by He flow to remove the loosely adsorbed components. Effluents of

C2H2and CO2were detected after heating the system to 393K(Figure 7a). Negligible amounts of C2H2and CO2were eluted from the bed after changing the sweeping gas of He to C2H4(Figure 7b). Further He sweeping was performed until no more gas was detected. C2H2and CO2, but no C2H4, were detected in the final heating stage, thus confirming the preferred selection of C2H2and CO2compared with C2H4by the molecular trap in NTU-67. In fact, only a small amount of adsorbed C2H4was adsorbed in NTU-67@C2H4that can also be replaced by the C2H2/CO2mixture (Figure 7c,d).

When the gas feed changed to CO2/C2H4(5 mL min−1 , 50/50, v/v) (Figure 8b), pure C2H4was also detected at first, while, CO2was absorbed. This means the polymer-grade C2H4(> 99.95%)can be harvested in 11.5  and 12.1  min in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni, which are far shorter than that of NTU-67 (27.0 min). Given the single gas isotherms and stronger host- C2H2interactions,

we can rationally infer that the separation ability is based on thermodynamics in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni, making them be good purifier for C2H4from C2H2contained binary mixture, but not from the ternary mixture of C2H2/CO2/C2H4.

2.11. Stability Evaluation

The adsorbent should own good water stability, which is necessary for practical application.[22] Due to the alkaline solutioninduced crystal conversion, the stability of NTU-67 is strongly expected. After treating the crystals in an acid-based solution (MATH), 7, and 12) at 373 K for 4 days or at 298 K for 120 days, respectively, the crystallinity, morphology, pore volume, and pore size distribution of NTU-67 were analyzed (Figure 9a, Figure S71–S73 and Table S4, Supporting Information). From the PXRD, nearly all peak positions are same with the as-synthesized phase. Meanwhile, we also note the intensity change of some peaks, such as the peak at 13.3°and 24.7°for the samples of NTU-67 (MATH), 373 K, 4 days and pH = 12, 373 K, 4 days). This may be due to the partial change of the exposed crystal plane during high-temperature treatment. In addition, CO2uptakes and pore size distribution of the treated samples are slightly higher or larger than that of the as-synthesized phase, as the generated tiny cracks of the treated crystals, validated by SEM images. In contrast, SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni totally lost their crystallinity after chemical treatment, while UTSA-300 dissolved in all solution immediately at room temperature (Figure S74, Supporting Information). Moreover, after all breakthrough experiments, the NTU-67 also keeps the same diffraction with original peaks. In light of these, a breakthrough experiment of CO2/C2H2/C2H4(1/9/90, v/v/v)with water vapor (relative humidity: 22%) was also conducted. The breakpoints of C2H4and C2H2were same as for the curves with dry feed gas, however, the breakpoint of CO2becomes a little earlier when compared with that of the measurement under dry gas. Further cycle measurements under moisture reveal that same curves were observed, despite it has vapor uptake (Figure  9b and Figure S76, Supporting Information). Keeping the structures and preparation method in mind, this excellent stability should be assigned as a reduction in the framework energy

state by the boiling alkaline aqueous solution treatment,[23] as well as the stronger coordination between IM N and the Cu center. Consequently, a synthetic methodology for preparation of robust PCPs is developed.

3. Conclusion

Adsorption-based gas purification from multicomponent mixtures offers a very good opportunity to replace the conventional energy-consuming separation process, the requirements being a porous material having integrated properties of simultaneous adsorption selectivity toward one component, high capacity, and excellent stability. Using the post-synthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution, we achieved these required factors in NTU-67, a new trapand-flow crystal. Crystallographic studies under pure gas and mixed gases validate the positive effect of the molecular trap for C2H2and CO2capture. Further Ab calculations and blowing tests reveal that linear molecules of C2H2and CO2diffuse much faster than the butterfly-like C2H4in flow channel B. In addition, the interchannel window between channels A and B allows the gas to flow into the molecular trap existing in channel A. More interestingly, the three-bladed array of the trap and flow channels promotes the crystal to afford increased kinetic selectivity. This unique and promising architecture allows highly efficient polymer-grade C2H4purification from C2H2/CO2/C2H4mixtures under dynamic condition, even in the presence of moisture, at high temperature and with a wide gas ratio. Meanwhile, it is worthy to note that the robustness of the NTU-67 framework reflects that crystal conversion in hot water or chemical solution is a good choice to establish stable PCPs. Therefore, our findings, specifically, the record C2H4productivity achieved here, coupled with molecular-level insight gained into the trap-and-flow channels, offer an innovative route for the design of advanced physisorbents for further challenging separations.

Shape- and Size-Dependent Kinetic Ethylene Sieving from a Ternary Mixture by a Trap-and-Flow Channel Crystal

Qiubing Dong, Yuhang Huang, Kim Hyeon-Deuk, I-Ya Chang, Jingmeng Wan, Changlin Chen, Jingui Duan,* Wanqin Jin, and Susumu Kitagawa*

Ethylene (C2H4)purification from multicomponent mixtures by physical adsorption presents a great challenge in the chemical industry. This work successfully uses the postsynthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution to synthesize a trap-and-flow channel crystal (namely NTU-67), the flow channel of which provides an effective shape- and sizedependent sieving path for linear molecules such as acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2), while the adjacent channel possesses customized space for efficient molecular trapping. The three-bladed array of the nanospace enables the crystal to afford a record productivity of C2H4(121.5 mL g−1 , (MATH)from 22/2/24(7/9/90, v/v/v)mixtures in a single adsorption–desorption cycle under humid and dynamic conditions, even at a high temperature of 343 K and wide gas ratio. The molecular-level insight and mechanism of the cooperative role of the trap-and-flow channel, found computationally and observed experimentally, demonstrates a new design philosophy toward extending the application boundaries of porous coordination polymers to further challenging tasks.

1. Introduction

Separations by porous materials is a crucial process in our daily lives as well as in industry.[1] For example, zeolite adsorbents in respirators can increase the oxygen concentration to meet medical standards,[2] while activated carbons are used as typical adsorbents for water purification.[3] However, a most challenging process in industry is the separation of light

Ethylene (C2H4)is a typical light hydrocarbon and essential building block. It has been reported that in 2021 the global requirement for C2H4was 220–230 million tons. There are also reports of the oxidative coupling of methane for C2H4production.[5] However, in addition to C2H4formation, the byproducts of acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2)are also generated.[6] Therefore, the selective removal of the two impurities C2H2and CO2is crucial for the recovery of polymer-grade C2H4from a ternary mixture of C2H2/CO2/C2H4because C2H2can poison the catalyst during C2H4polymerization while CO2reduces the

quality of the polyethylene (PE).[7] Current industrial separation technology mainly adopts multistep purification processes, including chemical adsorption of CO2(with associated huge solvent waste) and catalytic hydrogenation of C2H2(involving the use of noble-metal catalysts at high pressure/temperature),[8] wherein the energy consumption is huge.

Physical adsorption offers a potential solution for energyefficient separation.[9] It is noteworthy that although good separation of binary mixtures, including C2H2/C2H4[10]and C2H2/CO2[11]mixtures, is achieved by using adsorbents under ambient conditions, C2H4purification from CO2and C2H2contained in ternary mixtures presents a great challenge, as there is a lack of physisorbents that can selectively capture CO2/C2H2over C2H4. [12] A possible solution is the application of synergistic sorbent separation technology (SSST), by packing two or more physisorbents together.[13] Nevertheless, exploring the use of a single adsorbent that can exclude C2H4from a ternary mixture is considered most desirable. In addition, addressing the practical problem of determining the arrangement order and weight ratio of the corresponding adsorbents of the SSST also warrants attention.

Porous coordination polymers (PCPs), assembled from an organic linker and inorganic node, are a new type of crystalline material that exhibits significant ability to be tuned in nanopore chemistry for gas separation applications.[9b,14] Generally, in a sieving mechanism, the focus is on the use of differences

[Figure: Scheme 1. Schematic of the trap-and-flow channel crystal that allows shape- and size-dependent kinetic sieving and molecular trapping for highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture.]

in gas sizes, found in rigid PCPs with narrow apertures—only the molecule with the smaller size is adsorbed, while the molecule with the larger size is excluded.[9c,15] But the competitive host–guest interactions of two or more impurities in such a fitted porous system confound the adsorption equilibrium, especially in a tandem 1D channel. PCPs with framework dynamics are regarded as another platform for multicomponent separation because the corresponding response can enable the material to distinguish small differences within the multicomponent,[16] but the external conditions need to be accurately controlled (e.g., specific temperature, pressure, and gas ratio), and further coadsorption may occur once the pore is opened. Kinetic-dependent molecular diffusion has also been proposed for gas separation by creating sites of local motion in the crystal.[17] However, when the number of components in the gas mixture increases to three or more, special recognition devices are required in the channels.

In this work, we installed a three-bladed trap-and-flow channel in a crystal and were then subsequently able to achieve highly efficient C2H4purification from a ternary mixture that contained CO2and C2H2, even in the presence of moisture, and at a high temperature and wide gas ratio (Scheme 1). The flow channel featuring an optimized window aperture can kinetically distinguish between linear molecules of CO2or C2H2and a butterflylike molecule of C2H4while the trap in another channel allows the efficient capture of adsorbed molecules, as was determined computationally and observed experimentally at molecular level. In addition, the crystal synthesis in boiling alkaline solution offered excellent robustness under hot acid/base conditions.

2. Results and Discussion

2.1. Synthesis and Structural Characterization

The crystal transformation of NTU-65 in alkaline aqueous solution at 100°Cafforded a polyhedral-shaped crystal (NTU-67) (Figure S1, Supporting Information). This is mainly based on the consideration that crystal conversion in an aqueous solution may tailor nanopore in light of the size of the water template and inherit functional sites to a greater extent. Crystal transformation in alkaline aqueous may also reduce the energy state of the generated framework, realizing the assembly of chemically robust structure.[18] Direct synthesis of NTU-67 has also been attempted by tuning conditions and other solvent-triggered crystal conversions, but these attempts were unsuccessful.

Crystal analysis revealed that NTU-67 crystallizes in the space group of R32, where the asymmetric unit includes onehalf Cu2+cation, one-half SiF62-anion, and one L1 ligand, thus giving the same formula (MATH)·xSolvent) with that of NTU-65 (Table S1 and Figure S4, Supporting Information). In NTU-67, each ligand and SiF62-anion was connected by two Cu atoms, respectively, and each Cu2+cation was bridged by two F atoms from two SiF62-ions and four imidazoles (IM) N atoms from four ligands. The two F atoms in the para position of the SiF62-ion join the octahedral coordination of the two adjacent Cu2+cations to establish an inorganic helical chain along the axis. Therefore, the self-catenated square grid sheets formed between Cu2+cations and organic linkers are further connected by this chain to establish a three-dimensional (3D) framework (Figure S5, Supporting Information). Further topology analysis revealed that NTU-67 features a mmo net after subsuming the doubly connected ligands and SiF62-ions into the sixfold-connected Cu nodes, forming a new group of porous isomers with NTU-65 (pcu) (Figure 1a,b; Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information). Interestingly, two face-shared triangular channels (A and B) were observed in this new framework. Channel B with the narrowest hole of 3.4 Acan be considered a nanochannel for diffusion-promoted kinetic selectivities of CO2/C2H4and C2H2/C2H4. The limited space (MATH)that is regulated by three SiF62-anions and six IMs in Channel A can be regarded as a molecular trap for preferred adsorption. In addition, the arrangement of the molecular trap and nanochannel is trifoliate and interconnected (Figure  1c–j; Figures  S8 and  S9, Supporting Information). Calculated by Platon, the ideal porosity of NTU-67 is 28.4%. The structures and phase purities of the as-synthesized and activated NTU-67 were confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis and Le-Bail analysis (Figures  S10 and S11, Supporting Information). The thermogravimetric analysis collected from 25°Cto 300°Cshowed that the structure of NTU-67 was thermally stable up to 250°C, confirmed by variable temperature PXRD (Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information).

2.5. Crystallographic Study under Mixture

To explore the competitive binding of the gases, we analyzed the crystal structure of NTU-67 exposed to CO2/C2H4(2/8, v/v, 1 bar, 298 K). Of note here is that a mixture of C2H2/C2H4cannot be distinguished by X-ray diffraction measurement. Interestingly, one CO2molecule that interacts with F atoms was found in the molecular trap of channel A, while a unique onedimensional (1D) array of CO2and C2H4was found in channels B (Figure 4). This observation offers support that CO2is more preferentially adsorbed by the molecular trap, even under relative low partial pressure. In addition, 1D molecular array confirms that channel B provides an effective flow channel. This is a rare observation of competitive binding of the gases by a molecule-level crystallographic study.

2.6. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Aperture of Channels A and B

To determine the origin of the effective molecular sieving for a gas mixture through NTU-67, we performed ab initio

The largest pore size (indicated by the red ball in channel A (Figure  5d,e) is only 0.92 Å, which is much smaller than the molecular sizes of CO2, C2H2, and C2H4. Thus, all of these three gases can hardly pass through channel A. This result agrees well with the existence of a separated and isolated space in channel A (Figure 1d). The effective pore size of channel B was estimated on the three different cross sections, namely the center cross-section, the entrance cross-section, and the lower cross-section (Figure 5f–i). The red balls in Figure 5g–i express the vdW radius of a C atom (≈ 1.7 Å )for comparison. A comparison of Figure 5g,h indicates that there is a bottleneck going through channel B; there is a hole at the entrance cross-section of ≈ 3 . 4 Åin size. CO2and C2H2, with molecular sizes 3.40 and 3.68 Å, respectively, can pass through channel B, taking into account fluctuation and deformation of the channel structure. The hole size can be even larger than the molecular size of C2H2, depending on a time-dependent instantaneous channel structure. This means that structural modulation and deformation of the channel structure can play a critical role in molecular flow in NTU-67. In contrast, due to the restricted space, C2H4(molecular size 4.30 Å) passes through channel B with much more difficulty than CO2and C2H2.

Of even greater importance is the following. To pass through channel B, linear molecules such as C2H2and CO2should be aligned in wavy lines, as indicated in Figure  5j. 2.7. Ab Initio Calculation of Functional Molecular Trap

To support the molecular trap scenario discussed above, we performed ab initio calculations for the adsorption energy of C2H2and C2H4. The numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H4and channel B·C2H4are higher than the numbers of bonds formed in channel A–C2H2and channel B·C2H2, respectively (Figures S36–S38, Supporting Information). We note that the computationally obtained bond distance is shorter than the experimentally observed bond distance, as the former corresponds to the minimum energy structure calculated at 0Kwhile the latter includes thermal fluctuation and structural disorder at 298 K. We then selected three SiF62-ions and a gas molecule to calculate the adsorption energy because SiF62-ions are the most important and essential adsorption sites (Figures  S40 and S41, Supporting Information). The resulting adsorption energy of C2H2is higher than that of C2H4(in channel A 1.5 times and in channel B 1.25 times). The C2H2-involved bond distance is shorter than the C2H4-involved bond distance, in both channels A and B. The shorter distance

overcomes the order of the numbers of bonds and makes the adsorption energy of C2H2higher than the adsorption energy of C2H4. The faster flow and the higher adsorption energy enable C2H2to locate molecular traps existing in channel A more effectively than C2H4, leading to the sieving separation of C2H4from a C2H2/C2H4mixture. These computational insights are in good agreement with the experimental observations of the isosteric enthalpy and the gas-loaded crystal analysis, as well as with the higher adsorption rates of C2H2compared with C2H4as seen in Figures 2–4.

2.8. Improved Kinetic Selectivity Achieved with a Three-Bladed Array

To validate the collaborative roles of the nanospace, the adsorption kinetics of each gas were evaluated on NTU-67 at 298 K (Figure 6; Figures S42 and S43, Supporting Information). The pressure change indicates that the adsorption rate of CO2is much higher than that of C2H4. The kinetic selectivity of CO2/C2H4is 5.26, while that of C2H2/C2H4is 3.86. For comparison, adsorption kinetics of the gases were also collected in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the framework with the same SiF62-ion and a square window aperture. The kinetic selectivities of both CO2/C2H4(3.50) and C2H2/C2H4(2.49) in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i are lower than on NTU-67. The advantages of NTU-67 can be rationalized by the enhanced CO2and C2H2diffusion and molecular trapping by the three-bladed array. As computationally indicated above, the nanochannel allows CO2and C2H2to smoothly flow along channel B, while the molecular trap provides effective trapping sites for them, resulting in the current dynamic sieving in NTU-67. In contrast, because adsorption sites and flow paths exist in the same 1D channel in SIFSIX-2-Cu-i, the adsorbed molecules occupy the limited space in the 1D channel, making it difficult for subsequent molecules to pass through.

2.9. Molecular Trapping Effect

Based on the different trap–guest interactions and size effect, as well as the computational insights supporting them, the effect of molecular trapping was explored under dynamic conditions. The adsorbent should own good water stability, which is necessary for practical application.[22] Due to the alkaline solutioninduced crystal conversion, the stability of NTU-67 is strongly expected. Meanwhile, we also note the intensity change of some peaks, such as the peak at 13.3°and 24.7°for the samples of NTU-67 (MATH), 373 K, 4 days and pH = 12, 373 K, 4 days). This may be due to the partial change of the exposed crystal plane during high-temperature treatment. In contrast, SIFSIX-2-Cu-i and SIFSIX-17-Ni totally lost their crystallinity after chemical treatment, while UTSA-300 dissolved in all solution immediately at room temperature (Figure S74, Supporting Information). In light of these, a breakthrough experiment of CO2/C2H2/C2H4(1/9/90, v/v/v)with water vapor (relative humidity: 22%) was also conducted. 3. Conclusion

Adsorption-based gas purification from multicomponent mixtures offers a very good opportunity to replace the conventional energy-consuming separation process, the requirements being a porous material having integrated properties of simultaneous adsorption selectivity toward one component, high capacity, and excellent stability. Using the post-synthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution, we achieved these required factors in NTU-67, a new trapand-flow crystal. Crystallographic studies under pure gas and mixed gases validate the positive effect of the molecular trap for C2H2and CO2capture. Further Ab calculations and blowing tests reveal that linear molecules of C2H2and CO2diffuse much faster than the butterfly-like C2H4in flow channel B. In addition, the interchannel window between channels A and B allows the gas to flow into the molecular trap existing in channel A. More interestingly, the three-bladed array of the trap and flow channels promotes the crystal to afford increased kinetic selectivity. This unique and promising architecture allows highly efficient polymer-grade C2H4purification from C2H2/CO2/C2H4mixtures under dynamic condition, even in the presence of moisture, at high temperature and with a wide gas ratio. Meanwhile, it is worthy to note that the robustness of the NTU-67 framework reflects that crystal conversion in hot water or chemical solution is a good choice to establish stable PCPs. Therefore, our findings, specifically, the record C2H4productivity achieved here, coupled with molecular-level insight gained into the trap-and-flow channels, offer an innovative route for the design of advanced physisorbents for further challenging separations.

Shape- and Size-Dependent Kinetic Ethylene Sieving from a Ternary Mixture by a Trap-and-Flow Channel Crystal

Qiubing Dong, Yuhang Huang, Kim Hyeon-Deuk, I-Ya Chang, Jingmeng Wan, Changlin Chen, Jingui Duan,* Wanqin Jin, and Susumu Kitagawa*

Ethylene (C2H4)purification from multicomponent mixtures by physical adsorption presents a great challenge in the chemical industry. This work successfully uses the postsynthetic method of crystal transformation in boiling alkaline solution to synthesize a trap-and-flow channel crystal (namely NTU-67), the flow channel of which provides an effective shape- and sizedependent sieving path for linear molecules such as acetylene (C2H2)and carbon dioxide (CO2), while the adjacent channel possesses customized space for efficient molecular trapping. The three-bladed array of the nanospace enables the crystal to afford a record productivity of C2H4(121.5 mL g−1 , (MATH)from 22/2/24(7/9/90, v/v/v)mixtures in a single adsorption–desorption cycle under humid and dynamic conditions, even at a high temperature of 343 K and wide gas ratio. The molecular-level insight and mechanism of the cooperative role of the trap-and-flow channel, found computationally and observed experimentally, demonstrates a new design philosophy toward extending the application boundaries of porous coordination polymers to further challenging tasks.

1. Introduction

Separations by porous materials is a crucial process in our daily lives as well as in industry.[1] For example, zeolite adsorbents in respirators can increase the oxygen concentration to meet medical standards,[2] while activated carbons are used as typical adsorbents for water purification.[3] However, a most challenging process in industry is the separation of light
