## Introduction

Metal-Organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous materials prepared with metal nodes and ligands . The porous structure is integrated with functionality of building blocks to improve the applications of MOFs significantly . The pore apertures provide surface and space to realize high adsorption capacity and to differentiate the molecular species with different size . Yaghi et al pioneered that the rigid ligands with different struts, including biphenyl, tetrahydropyrene, pyrene, and terphenyl, were used to realize the controllable pore of MOFs . However, the rigid aromatic ligands are not perfect to extend the pore size due to the large size themselves.

Antenna effect is observed from lanthanide complexes and MOFs . Organic ligand severs as an “antenna” to absorb photons and generates its triplet state (T1) via intersystem crossing (ISC) from singlet state (S1) . The triplet state sensitizes Ln3+ ions to achieve their characteristic emission . Unique luminescent properties are realized, including high quantum yield, large Stokes shift, and bright visible emission . However, the energy level of S1 and T1 is critically limited, so carboxyl benzene is often used to prepare Ln-MOFs with antenna effect emission. Reversely, the π-conjugation structure of polycyclic aromatic ligands decreases the energy level of T1 to forbid energy transfer for the excitation of Ln3+ ions. We have introduced nitrogen atoms into tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)-ethylene to tune the energy level of the ligand, but only the characteristic emission of Eu3+ was excited . Thus, antenna effect and large-pore are seemingly a dilemma for MOFs.

If carboxyl benzenes are connected together through flexible single bond as flexible ligands, the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained, while the size of the ligands are enlarged. Thus, the MOFs with big pore may be prepared, while the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained for antenna effect emission. Flexible ligand is a breakthrough to the traditional opinion that rigid ligands are used to prepare MOFs . As the third generation of porous coordination polymers , flexible MOFs integrate multiple functionality and improve the structure of MOFs to realize dynamic guest inclusion and removal, breathing for reversible response . Thus, flexible MOFs become an important strategy to improve properties and extend applications by taking the advantage of specific structure.

Herein, we developed a flexible ligand to prepare the MOFs with antenna effect and big pore, simultaneously. To this end, trefoil flexible ligand, 1,3,5-tris(5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1) was prepared by attaching three isophthalic acids (L2) to a benzene ring through flexible –CH2-O- group . The flexible Ln-MOF single crystalline was successfully prepared although it is difficult owing to the disorder and the uncertainty of the preparation process . Single crystal result revealed that the aperture is enlarged to 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL for L1-Eu MOF. Moreover, antenna effect emission is observed from L1-Eu and L1-Tb MOFs . The flexible single bond is used to connect isophthalic acid and benzene ring, so L1 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, similar to L2. Moreover, the –CH2-O- group tunes the energy transfer, so L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission at 360 nm and 623 nm under single excitation of 290 nm for ratiometric detection of PO4 3- and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP). Less works studied the effect of porous structure of MOFs on target entrance and linear response range for the analytical purpose. We found small pore of MOFs results in poor linear response because of the different diffusion dynamics of a target at different concentrations. The relative specific surface area affects the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to expand the aperture, improve optical properties, and study the response mechanism for the extensive applications.

## Synthesis of 1,3,5-tris (5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1)

L1 was synthesized according to the previous work . In a typical reaction, a mixture of dimethyl-5-hydroxyisophthalate (2.6 g, 0.0125 mol), KI (23 mg, 0.15 mmol), K2CO3 (6.9 g, 0.05 mol) in DMF (50 mL) was heated to 100 °C for 1 h. 1,3,5-tris (bromomethyl) benzene (0.89 g, 0.0025 mol) was dissolved in DMF (3 mL), added in the above solution drop-wise in 3 min, and heated at 100 °C for 3 h. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and then poured into water to produce a white precipitate. After filtering and washing with ice cold water, the solid was dried in an oven at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 82%). The methyl ester product was dissolved in methanol (40 mL), and an aqueous NaOH solution (2.4 g in 40 mL H2O) was added, 80 °C reflux for 12 h. Then, methanol was evaporated. The solution was acidified to pH 1–2 with HCl (8 M). The precipitate was washed with H2O and dried at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 93%).

## Synthesis of L1-Ln MOFs

Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (27 mg, 0.06 mmol) and L1 (13 mg, 0.02 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 2.0 mL), ultrapure water (2.0 mL) and formic acid (HCOOH 0.2 mL). After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 100 °C for 5 days. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the product was washed with water and ethanol to remove the residual L1 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the sample of L1-Eu MOF was obtained. The synthesis of L1-Tb MOF and L1-Gd MOF was similar to that of L1-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Synthesis of L2-Ln MOFs

L2-Eu MOF was synthesized according to the former work . Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (44.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) and L2 (16.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 7.0 mL) and ultrapure water (3.0 mL). The as-obtained mixture was transferred to a stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave of 30 mL capacity. After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 150 °C for 12 h. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the solution was removed by centrifugation and the product was washed with DMF and ethanol to remove the residual L2 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. The synthesis of L2-Tb MOF and L2-Gd MOF was similar to that of L2-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Detection of PO4 3- or ATP

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared Na3PO4 solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 70 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm. The fluorescence detection of L2-Eu MOF and L1-Tb MOF for PO4 3- is same as that of the detection of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-. L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared ATP solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 50 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm.

## Chemical stability test of L1-Eu MOF upon water, acid and base

L1-Eu MOF sample (10 mg for each solvent) was added to different pH aqueous solutions. After immersed for 24 h, the solids were taken out and dried at 60 °C for PXRD data collection.

## Reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in PO4 3- (10 μM) to obtain 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. After fluorescence detection, the material was washed with ultrapure water and dired at 60 °C. The recycled material was used for fluorescence detection and PXRD data collection. We studied the reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3- through the process for five times.

## Detection of targets in real samples

The water samples were collected from the Xinkai lake and tap water of Nankai University (Tianjin, China). The lake water was treated with a 0.22 μm filter membrane to remove impurities. A series of water samples containing different concentrations of PO4 3- were prepared by adding different volumes of 0.1 mM PO4 3- standard solution. The fluorescence spectra were tested after the intensity stabilized. Serum samples were selected as a system to detect ATP.

## Structure and energy level of L1

Flexible ligands break the opinion that rigid ligands are used for MOFs. The different modules are connected together through single bonds , so flexible ligands own the properties of the modules and enlarged size, simultaneously. Correspondingly, the functionality of the MOFs is improved significantly. L2 can effectively sensitize Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, but the pore of L2-Eu MOF is almost completely blocked . Thus, we connected three L2 to benzene ring through –CH2-O- chains to form tri-isophthalate flexible ligand, L1. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and mass spectrometric results confirmed that L1 was successfully prepared . The structure of L1 was illustrated in and expected to retain the optical properties of L2 and expand its size to prepare MOFs with large pore and antenna effect, simultaneously.

Density functional theory (DFT) calculation was first used to reveal the energy level of L1 and L2 . The energy gap between the HOMO and LUMO of L1 is lessened to 4.77 from 5.67 eV of L2. The smaller energy gap results in less energy for electron transition. This was validated with their UV–vis absorption and solid fluorescence. The UV–vis absorption peak of L2 is 280 nm and redshifts to 310 nm for L1 . The solid fluorescence is red-shifted from 360 nm (L2) to 415 nm (L1) . The absorption and fluorescence illustrated that the energy level of L1 is still efficient to sensitize Ln3+ as no big π-conjugation structure forms.

## Preparation and characterization of L1-Ln MOFs

Ln3+ (Eu3+, Tb3+, or Gd3+) and L1 were dissolved in the mixture of DMF/water and then reacted at 100 °C for 5 days with the help of formic acid to prepare L1-Ln MOFs (the detail is listed in SI). Moreover, we obtained the Ln-MOFs single-crystalline . The three MOFs show the same PXRD patterns that agree well with the simulated result, so they show the same structures with high crystallinity ( A). L1-Eu MOF was therefore selected to discuss the structure with single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis results. L1-Eu MOF crystallizes in hexagonal system with the P-62c space group. The asymmetric unit of L1-Eu MOF contains one crystallography independent Eu(III) ions, half of a L1 ligand, half of a bridged oxygen ions of completely deprotonated μ3-O, one dimethylamine cation, and one coordinate water molecules. L1 ligand adopts three distinct coordination modes including bidentate chelate mode, bidentate bridging mode and bidentate 1,3-chelating mode (B). Also, three of nona-coordinated Eu(III) ions share on mutual oxygen center, which further synergizes nine carboxyl groups and three terminal water molecules to construct a tri-core secondary building unit (SBU) (C). The overall framework structure exhibits a three-dimensional (3D) matrix of honeycomb-shape constituted by hexagonal channels with the pore size of ∼18 Å along the c axis (D). It is worth noting that, as far as we know, L1-Eu MOF can be regard as an unprecedented (6, 9)-connected topology net with a point symbol of {411.64}3{430.66}2 which named as nkxyz (Nankai University, Xia, Yin and Zhang) .

L1-Eu MOF exhibits a rod-like structure with the size of ∼3 μm. EDS mapping results reveal the uniform element distribution in the single crystal ( A). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) shows that the frameworks of L1-Ln MOFs are stable until 400 °C. 19.6% of residual solvents are lost at first. The frameworks begin to collapse over 400 °C to leave the oxides with the loss of L1 ligand, demonstrating their high thermal stability (B). Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra of L1 and the MOFs are tested (C). The absorption band of L1 at around 1,710 cm−1 is attributed to the C=O stretching vibration, but a redshift is observed in MOFs. In addition, the broad bands at 2,500–3,000 cm−1 still appears fully in MOFs, so L1 is partly deprotonated to form the MOFs, similar to the single crystal result. The MOFs form through the coordination of –COOH and Ln3+ ions. To evaluate the permanent porosity of L1-Eu MOF, the sample was guest-exchanged with methanol (CH3OH) and activated by supercritical carbon dioxide fluid to yield the guest-free phase. Then, N2 adsorption isotherms were measured. Based on the N2 adsorption data, the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of L1-Eu MOF is 580 m2/g (D) and the pore size is approximately 18 Å (E), which is consistent with the simulated crystal structure . Eu is a heavy atom with high atomic mass, so the big size of L1 ligand plays an important role for the large pore and low density. L2-Eu MOF has also been successfully synthesized. As shown in , the absorption peak of L2 at 1715 cm−1 is attributed to the stretching vibration of C = O, while there is no peak of C = O in L2-Eu MOF, proving the coordination of –COOH and Eu3+, which is consistent with literature reports . As a comparison, the pores of L2-Eu MOF are almost blocked because of the strong steric hindrance with two carboxylic acid groups in the meta position. To verify the robustness of L1-Ln MOFs, the MOFs were immersed in aqueous solutions with pH from 4 to 11. The framework is remained within 24 h at room temperature, illustrating their good chemical stability (A). In addition, L1-Eu MOF was soaked in aqueous solution for 3, 5 and 7 days. B shows that the structure is still intact. Because the strong coordination interaction between carboxyl groups and Ln3+ ions as well as the strong covalent bond in the flexible ligand, the aqueous stability of L1-Eu MOF was therefore confirmed. Thus, L1-Eu MOF shows high stability, high porosity, and low density even flexible ligand is used.

## Antenna effect emission and optical properties of MOFs

The energy level of L1, L2, Eu3+, Tb3+, and Gd3+ ions was recorded to better understand how L1 assembled with three L2 ligands affect the emission behavior of Ln-MOFs . The singlet-state energy (S1) of L1 is 32258 cm−1 (310 nm), while that of L2 is 35714 cm−1 (280 nm). The triplet-state energy (T1) of L1 and L2 is 24813 cm−1 (403 nm) and 22779 cm−1 (439 nm), respectively. The energy gap (ΔE1) between S1 and T1 is 7445 cm−1 and 12935 cm−1 for L1 and L2 . According to Reinhold’s empirical rule, intersystem crossing (ISC) is effective when ΔE1 between S1 and T1 of a ligand is larger than 5000 cm−1. Thus, L1 and L2 can absorb photons to produce its triplet state through ISC efficiently. The antenna effect emission of L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs was then investigated. L1 sensitizes Tb3+ for its efficient antenna effect emission. Similarly, Eu3+ is efficiently excited for its characteristic emission. Interestingly, the emission of L1 is also observed from L1-Eu MOF. The energy gap (ΔE2) between T1 of L1 and the excited state of Eu3+ ions is larger than that of L2, so the incomplete energy transfer occurs for the dual-emission ( A). L2 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+, similar to the previous report (B) . Gd3+ owns higher excited state level and could not be excited by both L1 and L2 (A and 4B). The energy level and transfer between the two ligands and the Ln3+ ions are illustrated in C. L1 maintains the energy level of L2 to excite Eu3+ and Tb3+, while the flexible –CH2-O- group also achieves the strong dual-emission of L1-Eu MOF to facilitate ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visual detection. As a conclusion, the trefoil L1 ligand realizes the large pore size, low density, and the improved efficiency to sensitize both Eu3+ and Tb3+ for their antenna effect emission in the MOFs.

L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission, so its other optical properties are investigated in detail. The UV–vis absorption spectra of L1 and L1-Eu MOF are recorded (A). A strong absorption peak is observed at 310 nm from L1. However, two absorption peaks are observed at 290 nm and 334 nm from L1-Eu MOF. The peak at 334 nm is attributed to ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT). The emission at 290 nm blue-shifted is due to the twisted structure of L1 in MOFs. The fluorescence spectra of L1-Eu MOF are tested at the excitation wavelengths from 250 to 300 nm with the optimal excitation of 290 nm (B and S12C). The emission from L1 is observed at ∼ 360 nm under the excitation of 290 nm, but the intensity decreases because of the energy transfer to Eu3+ ions (D). Moreover, the strong characteristic emission of Eu3+ ions is observed at 596, 623, 656, and 704 nm from L1-Eu MOF, attributed to the typical f-f transitions of Eu3+ ions, as the transfer of 5D0-7F1, 5D0-7F2, 5D0-7F3, and 5D0-7F4, respectively. Thus, L1 is excited and then sensitizes Eu3+ ions with the antenna effect procedure. In addition, the fluorescence intensity of L1-Eu MOF in pH 3.0–9.0 aqueous system remains stable and the emission of L1-Eu MOF keeps unchanged for at least three days, which is conducive to the detection of targets in different conditions .

## Response of PO4 3- and ATP

Phosphate (PO4 3-) plays an important role in environmental system and biological processes . The high affinity between Ln3+ and PO4 3- has been proved . ATP contains three PO4 3- groups, so it can also interact with L1-Ln MOFs. L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs own different pore sizes, so the responses of different MOFs to PO4 3- and ATP were studied to develop the analytical method for PO4 3- and ATP and reveal the effect of pore size and specific area.

The structure of L1-Eu MOF remains unchanged after soaked in Na3PO4 solution for 24 h, revealing that it is extremely stable for PO4 3- detection . As the PO4 3- concentration increases, the emission of L1-Eu MOF at 360 nm enhances, while that at 623 nm decreases slightly ( A). The obvious color change is observed along with the PO4 3- concentration as shown in CIE chromaticity (B). In addition, a linear correlation is observed between the I 360/I 623 ratio and PO4 3- concentration in the range from 1.0 to 45.1 μM with a coefficient of R 2 = 0.987 (C and 5D). A limit of detection (LOD) of 0.183 μM is obtained for PO4 3- and lower than or the same as that of the other fluorescence methods .

As a comparison, the response of L1-Tb MOF to PO4 3- was recorded . Along with the increased PO4 3- content, the emission at 549 nm decreases, while that at 360 nm appears and increases gradually. The decreased emission from Tb ions and the enhanced L1 emission confirmed the antenna effect procedure with the energy transfer from the ligand to Ln3+ ions. The LOD is 7.52 μM and the linear range is 10.1–50.2 μM with the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549. However, the fluorescence change of L1-Tb MOF is indistinguishable for visual detection as illustrated in CIE chromaticity. Thus, L1-Eu MOF provides the possibility for ratiometric sensing and visible detection of PO4 3-. The self-calibration function of the dual-emission improves the sensitivity for PO4 3- with lower LOD than that from L1-Tb MOF.

To explore the selectivity of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3-, the competition experiments were performed for other anions. PO4 3- exhibits the remarkable fluorescence change than other anions ( A and B). The anti-interference capacity was tested with the coexistence of PO4 3- and other anions at four-fold concentration level. The response to PO4 3- is not affected by the interference anions (C and D). The PXRD patterns and fluorescence intensity ratio I 360/I 623 of L1-Eu MOF remain stable after five cycles upon the addition and removal of PO4 3- ions . With the formula of Qt = (C0-Ct)V/m, the adsorption capacity of L1-Eu MOF on PO4 3- was calculated to be 43 mg/g by ion chromatography, which was basically consistent with the result of fluorescence spectroscopy. Thus, L1-Eu MOF is promising for detecting PO4 3- with high selectivity and good recyclability as validated with the analysis of real samples .

The fluorescence response of L1-Eu MOF to ATP was studied. A favorable linearity is observed between the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549 and ATP concentration in the range from 2.0 to 24.9 μM. A low limit of detection (LOD) of ATP was obtained to be 0.147 μM , which owned a superior performance to most sensors for ATP detection . L1-Eu MOF was successfully used for the detection of ATP in real samples . The flexible ligand, L1, achieves the large-pore aperture to insert ATP molecules in the MOF for sensing purpose.

The response of L2-Eu MOF to PO4 3- was further studied as a comparison. The emission at 623 nm decreases slightly with the addition of PO4 3-. A poor linear relationship in the range of 5.0–49.6 μM PO4 3- is obtained with L2-Eu MOF as probe . The decrease in emission at 623 nm is attributed to the interaction of Eu3+ and PO4 3-.

## Response mechanisms

Different response speed and range is observed when MOFs are used as the probes. Similarly, we found different MOFs show different responses to PO4 3- and ATP. High structure stability was observed for L1-Eu MOF in PO4 3- solution. The emission of Eu3+ or Tb3+ decreases, while that from L1 enhances upon the addition of PO4 3-. The result confirmed that PO4 3- or ATP interact to the open sites in the MOFs as the interaction decreases the energy transfer to Eu ions for the increased intensity at 360 nm and the decreased emission at 623 nm. The interaction between Eu3+ and PO4 3- was confirmed with UV–Vis absorption, Infrared, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). As shown in A, after the addition of PO4 3-, the absorption peak of L1-Eu MOF is changed and closed to the absorption of L1. IR shows that the C = O of L1-Eu MOF at 1654 cm−1 blueshifts to 1723 cm−1 after incubation with an aqueous solution of PO4 3- (B). Meanwhile, XPS illustrates the presence of P 2 s after soaked in PO4 3- solution and the slight shift from 529.199 to 529.312 eV of O 1 s is observed ( C, D). In addition, the Eu 3d peaks also display a slight shift from 1132.298 to 1132.394 eV, suggesting the binding of Eu3+ to PO4 3- . Therefore, there is strong interactions between the P-O bonds of PO4 3- and Eu-O cluster. Moreover, as shown in , –COOH of L1 plays an important role in detecting PO4 3- or ATP. and B show that after soaking, the C = O absorption peak of L1 and L1-Eu MOF appear shift. Thus, the response of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3- and ATP is influenced by the affinity of Eu3+ to phosphate group and the interaction between L1 and phosphate group. With the formula of (F0-F)/F = Kb[Ladd] , we calculated that the binding constants of MOF and PO4 3- or ATP are 4.3 × 104 and 6.3 × 104, respectively. The concentration- and incubation time-dependent responses were then studied to reveal precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response.

L1-Eu MOF shows the same concentration-dependent response for PO4 3- and ATP at low concentration, while ATP exhibits a little high response than PO4 3- at high concentration level ( A). Short incubation time results in the same time-dependent response, but higher response is observed from ATP with long time over PO4 3- (B). The result indicates that not all of three phosphate groups in ATP interact to the open sites. However, almost no fluorescence response was observed to ATP for L2-Eu MOF as the small pore blocks ATP directly (C and 7D). The intensity increases from 0 to 10.0 μM quickly and then becomes slow for PO4 3- with L2-Eu MOF as the probe (C). The pore of L2-Eu MOF is small and blocked for the slow response for PO4 3- ions beyond 10 μM as different diffusion dynamics was observed for the target at different concentrations. ATP molecule was directly blocked because of its big size of ∼ 15 Å. Reversely, L1-Eu MOF owns the pore of 18 Å to allow PO4 3- and ATP entering easily. Thus, the pore size governs the response of the targets because the different diffusion dynamics was observed in L2-Eu MOF for PO4 3- at different concentrations, while ATP was blocked directly.

The mechanism could also be used to explain the linear response range. The linear range of 2.0–24.9 μM is observed for ATP with L1-Eu MOF as probe, narrower than 1.0–45.1 μM for PO4 3-. The same concentration-dependent trend was observed for the two targets (A). Thus, it is not the three phosphate groups that result in the narrow range of ATP, but its big size occupies larger area. The result in C illustrated that the MOFs with small pore exhibited poor linear response of PO4 3- because of the different diffuse dynamics at different concentrations. Thus, the big pore of MOFs improves the accessibility of the targets, while the big relative specific area enlarges the response range. In combination of the dual-emission from antenna effect procedure, the sensing efficiency is obviously improved with L1-Eu MOF as a probe.

## Conclusions

In conclusion, for the first time, we proposed that flexible ligand was used to expand the pore for MOFs and to realize antenna effect, simultaneously. To this end, three –CH2-O- chains were used to connect three L2 ligands to form flexible ligand L1 with a large size. L1 coordinated with Ln3+ ions to form MOFs. Single crystal results indicated that the pore size of L1-Eu MOF was enlarged to ∼ 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL. Moreover, the optical properties of L2 was retained in L1 and flexible –CH2-O- tuned the energy level of L1, so strong dual emission was observed from L1-Eu MOF. In combination with HOMO and LUMO level of L1 and L2, we validated the antenna effect emission. The dual-emission made L1-Eu MOF active as ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visible detection. Importantly, the precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response was revealed. The pore size affected the response through the accessibility of targets as different diffusion dynamics was observed. The targets with big size were blocked directly in the MOFs with small pore. The relative specific surface area affected the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to improve the functionality, to study the response mechanism, and to extend the applications of MOFs.

## Introduction

Metal-Organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous materials prepared with metal nodes and ligands . The porous structure is integrated with functionality of building blocks to improve the applications of MOFs significantly . The pore apertures provide surface and space to realize high adsorption capacity and to differentiate the molecular species with different size . Yaghi et al pioneered that the rigid ligands with different struts, including biphenyl, tetrahydropyrene, pyrene, and terphenyl, were used to realize the controllable pore of MOFs . However, the rigid aromatic ligands are not perfect to extend the pore size due to the large size themselves.

Antenna effect is observed from lanthanide complexes and MOFs . Organic ligand severs as an “antenna” to absorb photons and generates its triplet state (T1) via intersystem crossing (ISC) from singlet state (S1) . The triplet state sensitizes Ln3+ ions to achieve their characteristic emission . Unique luminescent properties are realized, including high quantum yield, large Stokes shift, and bright visible emission . However, the energy level of S1 and T1 is critically limited, so carboxyl benzene is often used to prepare Ln-MOFs with antenna effect emission. Reversely, the π-conjugation structure of polycyclic aromatic ligands decreases the energy level of T1 to forbid energy transfer for the excitation of Ln3+ ions. We have introduced nitrogen atoms into tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)-ethylene to tune the energy level of the ligand, but only the characteristic emission of Eu3+ was excited . Thus, antenna effect and large-pore are seemingly a dilemma for MOFs.

If carboxyl benzenes are connected together through flexible single bond as flexible ligands, the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained, while the size of the ligands are enlarged. Thus, the MOFs with big pore may be prepared, while the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained for antenna effect emission. Flexible ligand is a breakthrough to the traditional opinion that rigid ligands are used to prepare MOFs . As the third generation of porous coordination polymers , flexible MOFs integrate multiple functionality and improve the structure of MOFs to realize dynamic guest inclusion and removal, breathing for reversible response . Thus, flexible MOFs become an important strategy to improve properties and extend applications by taking the advantage of specific structure.

Herein, we developed a flexible ligand to prepare the MOFs with antenna effect and big pore, simultaneously. To this end, trefoil flexible ligand, 1,3,5-tris(5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1) was prepared by attaching three isophthalic acids (L2) to a benzene ring through flexible –CH2-O- group . The flexible Ln-MOF single crystalline was successfully prepared although it is difficult owing to the disorder and the uncertainty of the preparation process . Single crystal result revealed that the aperture is enlarged to 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL for L1-Eu MOF. Moreover, antenna effect emission is observed from L1-Eu and L1-Tb MOFs . The flexible single bond is used to connect isophthalic acid and benzene ring, so L1 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, similar to L2. Moreover, the –CH2-O- group tunes the energy transfer, so L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission at 360 nm and 623 nm under single excitation of 290 nm for ratiometric detection of PO4 3- and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP). Less works studied the effect of porous structure of MOFs on target entrance and linear response range for the analytical purpose. We found small pore of MOFs results in poor linear response because of the different diffusion dynamics of a target at different concentrations. The relative specific surface area affects the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to expand the aperture, improve optical properties, and study the response mechanism for the extensive applications.

## Synthesis of 1,3,5-tris (5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1)

L1 was synthesized according to the previous work . In a typical reaction, a mixture of dimethyl-5-hydroxyisophthalate (2.6 g, 0.0125 mol), KI (23 mg, 0.15 mmol), K2CO3 (6.9 g, 0.05 mol) in DMF (50 mL) was heated to 100 °C for 1 h. 1,3,5-tris (bromomethyl) benzene (0.89 g, 0.0025 mol) was dissolved in DMF (3 mL), added in the above solution drop-wise in 3 min, and heated at 100 °C for 3 h. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and then poured into water to produce a white precipitate. After filtering and washing with ice cold water, the solid was dried in an oven at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 82%). The methyl ester product was dissolved in methanol (40 mL), and an aqueous NaOH solution (2.4 g in 40 mL H2O) was added, 80 °C reflux for 12 h. Then, methanol was evaporated. The solution was acidified to pH 1–2 with HCl (8 M). The precipitate was washed with H2O and dried at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 93%).

## Synthesis of L1-Ln MOFs

Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (27 mg, 0.06 mmol) and L1 (13 mg, 0.02 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 2.0 mL), ultrapure water (2.0 mL) and formic acid (HCOOH 0.2 mL). After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 100 °C for 5 days. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the product was washed with water and ethanol to remove the residual L1 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the sample of L1-Eu MOF was obtained. The synthesis of L1-Tb MOF and L1-Gd MOF was similar to that of L1-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Synthesis of L2-Ln MOFs

L2-Eu MOF was synthesized according to the former work . Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (44.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) and L2 (16.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 7.0 mL) and ultrapure water (3.0 mL). The as-obtained mixture was transferred to a stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave of 30 mL capacity. After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 150 °C for 12 h. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the solution was removed by centrifugation and the product was washed with DMF and ethanol to remove the residual L2 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. The synthesis of L2-Tb MOF and L2-Gd MOF was similar to that of L2-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Detection of PO4 3- or ATP

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared Na3PO4 solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 70 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm. The fluorescence detection of L2-Eu MOF and L1-Tb MOF for PO4 3- is same as that of the detection of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-. L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared ATP solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 50 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm.

## Chemical stability test of L1-Eu MOF upon water, acid and base

L1-Eu MOF sample (10 mg for each solvent) was added to different pH aqueous solutions. After immersed for 24 h, the solids were taken out and dried at 60 °C for PXRD data collection.

## Reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in PO4 3- (10 μM) to obtain 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. After fluorescence detection, the material was washed with ultrapure water and dired at 60 °C. The recycled material was used for fluorescence detection and PXRD data collection. We studied the reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3- through the process for five times.

## Detection of targets in real samples

The water samples were collected from the Xinkai lake and tap water of Nankai University (Tianjin, China). The lake water was treated with a 0.22 μm filter membrane to remove impurities. A series of water samples containing different concentrations of PO4 3- were prepared by adding different volumes of 0.1 mM PO4 3- standard solution. The fluorescence spectra were tested after the intensity stabilized. Serum samples were selected as a system to detect ATP.

## Structure and energy level of L1

Flexible ligands break the opinion that rigid ligands are used for MOFs. The different modules are connected together through single bonds , so flexible ligands own the properties of the modules and enlarged size, simultaneously. Correspondingly, the functionality of the MOFs is improved significantly. L2 can effectively sensitize Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, but the pore of L2-Eu MOF is almost completely blocked . Thus, we connected three L2 to benzene ring through –CH2-O- chains to form tri-isophthalate flexible ligand, L1. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and mass spectrometric results confirmed that L1 was successfully prepared . The structure of L1 was illustrated in and expected to retain the optical properties of L2 and expand its size to prepare MOFs with large pore and antenna effect, simultaneously.

Density functional theory (DFT) calculation was first used to reveal the energy level of L1 and L2 . The energy gap between the HOMO and LUMO of L1 is lessened to 4.77 from 5.67 eV of L2. The smaller energy gap results in less energy for electron transition. This was validated with their UV–vis absorption and solid fluorescence. The UV–vis absorption peak of L2 is 280 nm and redshifts to 310 nm for L1 . The solid fluorescence is red-shifted from 360 nm (L2) to 415 nm (L1) . The absorption and fluorescence illustrated that the energy level of L1 is still efficient to sensitize Ln3+ as no big π-conjugation structure forms.

## Preparation and characterization of L1-Ln MOFs

Ln3+ (Eu3+, Tb3+, or Gd3+) and L1 were dissolved in the mixture of DMF/water and then reacted at 100 °C for 5 days with the help of formic acid to prepare L1-Ln MOFs (the detail is listed in SI). Moreover, we obtained the Ln-MOFs single-crystalline . The three MOFs show the same PXRD patterns that agree well with the simulated result, so they show the same structures with high crystallinity ( A). L1-Eu MOF was therefore selected to discuss the structure with single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis results. L1-Eu MOF crystallizes in hexagonal system with the P-62c space group. The asymmetric unit of L1-Eu MOF contains one crystallography independent Eu(III) ions, half of a L1 ligand, half of a bridged oxygen ions of completely deprotonated μ3-O, one dimethylamine cation, and one coordinate water molecules. L1 ligand adopts three distinct coordination modes including bidentate chelate mode, bidentate bridging mode and bidentate 1,3-chelating mode (B). Also, three of nona-coordinated Eu(III) ions share on mutual oxygen center, which further synergizes nine carboxyl groups and three terminal water molecules to construct a tri-core secondary building unit (SBU) (C). The overall framework structure exhibits a three-dimensional (3D) matrix of honeycomb-shape constituted by hexagonal channels with the pore size of ∼18 Å along the c axis (D). It is worth noting that, as far as we know, L1-Eu MOF can be regard as an unprecedented (6, 9)-connected topology net with a point symbol of {411.64}3{430.66}2 which named as nkxyz (Nankai University, Xia, Yin and Zhang) .

L1-Eu MOF exhibits a rod-like structure with the size of ∼3 μm. EDS mapping results reveal the uniform element distribution in the single crystal ( A). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) shows that the frameworks of L1-Ln MOFs are stable until 400 °C. 19.6% of residual solvents are lost at first. The frameworks begin to collapse over 400 °C to leave the oxides with the loss of L1 ligand, demonstrating their high thermal stability (B). Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra of L1 and the MOFs are tested (C). The absorption band of L1 at around 1,710 cm−1 is attributed to the C=O stretching vibration, but a redshift is observed in MOFs. In addition, the broad bands at 2,500–3,000 cm−1 still appears fully in MOFs, so L1 is partly deprotonated to form the MOFs, similar to the single crystal result. The MOFs form through the coordination of –COOH and Ln3+ ions. To evaluate the permanent porosity of L1-Eu MOF, the sample was guest-exchanged with methanol (CH3OH) and activated by supercritical carbon dioxide fluid to yield the guest-free phase. Then, N2 adsorption isotherms were measured. Based on the N2 adsorption data, the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of L1-Eu MOF is 580 m2/g (D) and the pore size is approximately 18 Å (E), which is consistent with the simulated crystal structure . Eu is a heavy atom with high atomic mass, so the big size of L1 ligand plays an important role for the large pore and low density. L2-Eu MOF has also been successfully synthesized. As shown in , the absorption peak of L2 at 1715 cm−1 is attributed to the stretching vibration of C = O, while there is no peak of C = O in L2-Eu MOF, proving the coordination of –COOH and Eu3+, which is consistent with literature reports . As a comparison, the pores of L2-Eu MOF are almost blocked because of the strong steric hindrance with two carboxylic acid groups in the meta position. To verify the robustness of L1-Ln MOFs, the MOFs were immersed in aqueous solutions with pH from 4 to 11. The framework is remained within 24 h at room temperature, illustrating their good chemical stability (A). In addition, L1-Eu MOF was soaked in aqueous solution for 3, 5 and 7 days. B shows that the structure is still intact. Because the strong coordination interaction between carboxyl groups and Ln3+ ions as well as the strong covalent bond in the flexible ligand, the aqueous stability of L1-Eu MOF was therefore confirmed. Thus, L1-Eu MOF shows high stability, high porosity, and low density even flexible ligand is used.

## Antenna effect emission and optical properties of MOFs

The energy level of L1, L2, Eu3+, Tb3+, and Gd3+ ions was recorded to better understand how L1 assembled with three L2 ligands affect the emission behavior of Ln-MOFs . The singlet-state energy (S1) of L1 is 32258 cm−1 (310 nm), while that of L2 is 35714 cm−1 (280 nm). The triplet-state energy (T1) of L1 and L2 is 24813 cm−1 (403 nm) and 22779 cm−1 (439 nm), respectively. The energy gap (ΔE1) between S1 and T1 is 7445 cm−1 and 12935 cm−1 for L1 and L2 . According to Reinhold’s empirical rule, intersystem crossing (ISC) is effective when ΔE1 between S1 and T1 of a ligand is larger than 5000 cm−1. Thus, L1 and L2 can absorb photons to produce its triplet state through ISC efficiently. The antenna effect emission of L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs was then investigated. L1 sensitizes Tb3+ for its efficient antenna effect emission. Similarly, Eu3+ is efficiently excited for its characteristic emission. Interestingly, the emission of L1 is also observed from L1-Eu MOF. The energy gap (ΔE2) between T1 of L1 and the excited state of Eu3+ ions is larger than that of L2, so the incomplete energy transfer occurs for the dual-emission ( A). L2 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+, similar to the previous report (B) . Gd3+ owns higher excited state level and could not be excited by both L1 and L2 (A and 4B). The energy level and transfer between the two ligands and the Ln3+ ions are illustrated in C. L1 maintains the energy level of L2 to excite Eu3+ and Tb3+, while the flexible –CH2-O- group also achieves the strong dual-emission of L1-Eu MOF to facilitate ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visual detection. As a conclusion, the trefoil L1 ligand realizes the large pore size, low density, and the improved efficiency to sensitize both Eu3+ and Tb3+ for their antenna effect emission in the MOFs.

L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission, so its other optical properties are investigated in detail. The UV–vis absorption spectra of L1 and L1-Eu MOF are recorded (A). A strong absorption peak is observed at 310 nm from L1. However, two absorption peaks are observed at 290 nm and 334 nm from L1-Eu MOF. The peak at 334 nm is attributed to ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT). The emission at 290 nm blue-shifted is due to the twisted structure of L1 in MOFs. The fluorescence spectra of L1-Eu MOF are tested at the excitation wavelengths from 250 to 300 nm with the optimal excitation of 290 nm (B and S12C). The emission from L1 is observed at ∼ 360 nm under the excitation of 290 nm, but the intensity decreases because of the energy transfer to Eu3+ ions (D). Moreover, the strong characteristic emission of Eu3+ ions is observed at 596, 623, 656, and 704 nm from L1-Eu MOF, attributed to the typical f-f transitions of Eu3+ ions, as the transfer of 5D0-7F1, 5D0-7F2, 5D0-7F3, and 5D0-7F4, respectively. Thus, L1 is excited and then sensitizes Eu3+ ions with the antenna effect procedure. In addition, the fluorescence intensity of L1-Eu MOF in pH 3.0–9.0 aqueous system remains stable and the emission of L1-Eu MOF keeps unchanged for at least three days, which is conducive to the detection of targets in different conditions .

## Response of PO4 3- and ATP

Phosphate (PO4 3-) plays an important role in environmental system and biological processes . The high affinity between Ln3+ and PO4 3- has been proved . ATP contains three PO4 3- groups, so it can also interact with L1-Ln MOFs. L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs own different pore sizes, so the responses of different MOFs to PO4 3- and ATP were studied to develop the analytical method for PO4 3- and ATP and reveal the effect of pore size and specific area.

The structure of L1-Eu MOF remains unchanged after soaked in Na3PO4 solution for 24 h, revealing that it is extremely stable for PO4 3- detection . As the PO4 3- concentration increases, the emission of L1-Eu MOF at 360 nm enhances, while that at 623 nm decreases slightly ( A). The obvious color change is observed along with the PO4 3- concentration as shown in CIE chromaticity (B). In addition, a linear correlation is observed between the I 360/I 623 ratio and PO4 3- concentration in the range from 1.0 to 45.1 μM with a coefficient of R 2 = 0.987 (C and 5D). A limit of detection (LOD) of 0.183 μM is obtained for PO4 3- and lower than or the same as that of the other fluorescence methods .

As a comparison, the response of L1-Tb MOF to PO4 3- was recorded . Along with the increased PO4 3- content, the emission at 549 nm decreases, while that at 360 nm appears and increases gradually. The decreased emission from Tb ions and the enhanced L1 emission confirmed the antenna effect procedure with the energy transfer from the ligand to Ln3+ ions. The LOD is 7.52 μM and the linear range is 10.1–50.2 μM with the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549. However, the fluorescence change of L1-Tb MOF is indistinguishable for visual detection as illustrated in CIE chromaticity. Thus, L1-Eu MOF provides the possibility for ratiometric sensing and visible detection of PO4 3-. The self-calibration function of the dual-emission improves the sensitivity for PO4 3- with lower LOD than that from L1-Tb MOF.

To explore the selectivity of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3-, the competition experiments were performed for other anions. PO4 3- exhibits the remarkable fluorescence change than other anions ( A and B). The anti-interference capacity was tested with the coexistence of PO4 3- and other anions at four-fold concentration level. The response to PO4 3- is not affected by the interference anions (C and D). The PXRD patterns and fluorescence intensity ratio I 360/I 623 of L1-Eu MOF remain stable after five cycles upon the addition and removal of PO4 3- ions . With the formula of Qt = (C0-Ct)V/m, the adsorption capacity of L1-Eu MOF on PO4 3- was calculated to be 43 mg/g by ion chromatography, which was basically consistent with the result of fluorescence spectroscopy. Thus, L1-Eu MOF is promising for detecting PO4 3- with high selectivity and good recyclability as validated with the analysis of real samples .

The fluorescence response of L1-Eu MOF to ATP was studied. A favorable linearity is observed between the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549 and ATP concentration in the range from 2.0 to 24.9 μM. A low limit of detection (LOD) of ATP was obtained to be 0.147 μM , which owned a superior performance to most sensors for ATP detection . L1-Eu MOF was successfully used for the detection of ATP in real samples . The flexible ligand, L1, achieves the large-pore aperture to insert ATP molecules in the MOF for sensing purpose.

The response of L2-Eu MOF to PO4 3- was further studied as a comparison. The emission at 623 nm decreases slightly with the addition of PO4 3-. A poor linear relationship in the range of 5.0–49.6 μM PO4 3- is obtained with L2-Eu MOF as probe . The decrease in emission at 623 nm is attributed to the interaction of Eu3+ and PO4 3-.

## Response mechanisms

Different response speed and range is observed when MOFs are used as the probes. Similarly, we found different MOFs show different responses to PO4 3- and ATP. High structure stability was observed for L1-Eu MOF in PO4 3- solution. The emission of Eu3+ or Tb3+ decreases, while that from L1 enhances upon the addition of PO4 3-. The result confirmed that PO4 3- or ATP interact to the open sites in the MOFs as the interaction decreases the energy transfer to Eu ions for the increased intensity at 360 nm and the decreased emission at 623 nm. The interaction between Eu3+ and PO4 3- was confirmed with UV–Vis absorption, Infrared, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). As shown in A, after the addition of PO4 3-, the absorption peak of L1-Eu MOF is changed and closed to the absorption of L1. IR shows that the C = O of L1-Eu MOF at 1654 cm−1 blueshifts to 1723 cm−1 after incubation with an aqueous solution of PO4 3- (B). Meanwhile, XPS illustrates the presence of P 2 s after soaked in PO4 3- solution and the slight shift from 529.199 to 529.312 eV of O 1 s is observed ( C, D). In addition, the Eu 3d peaks also display a slight shift from 1132.298 to 1132.394 eV, suggesting the binding of Eu3+ to PO4 3- . Therefore, there is strong interactions between the P-O bonds of PO4 3- and Eu-O cluster. Moreover, as shown in , –COOH of L1 plays an important role in detecting PO4 3- or ATP. and B show that after soaking, the C = O absorption peak of L1 and L1-Eu MOF appear shift. Thus, the response of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3- and ATP is influenced by the affinity of Eu3+ to phosphate group and the interaction between L1 and phosphate group. With the formula of (F0-F)/F = Kb[Ladd] , we calculated that the binding constants of MOF and PO4 3- or ATP are 4.3 × 104 and 6.3 × 104, respectively. The concentration- and incubation time-dependent responses were then studied to reveal precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response.

L1-Eu MOF shows the same concentration-dependent response for PO4 3- and ATP at low concentration, while ATP exhibits a little high response than PO4 3- at high concentration level ( A). Short incubation time results in the same time-dependent response, but higher response is observed from ATP with long time over PO4 3- (B). The result indicates that not all of three phosphate groups in ATP interact to the open sites. However, almost no fluorescence response was observed to ATP for L2-Eu MOF as the small pore blocks ATP directly (C and 7D). The intensity increases from 0 to 10.0 μM quickly and then becomes slow for PO4 3- with L2-Eu MOF as the probe (C). The pore of L2-Eu MOF is small and blocked for the slow response for PO4 3- ions beyond 10 μM as different diffusion dynamics was observed for the target at different concentrations. ATP molecule was directly blocked because of its big size of ∼ 15 Å. Reversely, L1-Eu MOF owns the pore of 18 Å to allow PO4 3- and ATP entering easily. Thus, the pore size governs the response of the targets because the different diffusion dynamics was observed in L2-Eu MOF for PO4 3- at different concentrations, while ATP was blocked directly.

The mechanism could also be used to explain the linear response range. The linear range of 2.0–24.9 μM is observed for ATP with L1-Eu MOF as probe, narrower than 1.0–45.1 μM for PO4 3-. The same concentration-dependent trend was observed for the two targets (A). Thus, it is not the three phosphate groups that result in the narrow range of ATP, but its big size occupies larger area. The result in C illustrated that the MOFs with small pore exhibited poor linear response of PO4 3- because of the different diffuse dynamics at different concentrations. Thus, the big pore of MOFs improves the accessibility of the targets, while the big relative specific area enlarges the response range. In combination of the dual-emission from antenna effect procedure, the sensing efficiency is obviously improved with L1-Eu MOF as a probe.

## Conclusions

In conclusion, for the first time, we proposed that flexible ligand was used to expand the pore for MOFs and to realize antenna effect, simultaneously. To this end, three –CH2-O- chains were used to connect three L2 ligands to form flexible ligand L1 with a large size. L1 coordinated with Ln3+ ions to form MOFs. Single crystal results indicated that the pore size of L1-Eu MOF was enlarged to ∼ 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL. Moreover, the optical properties of L2 was retained in L1 and flexible –CH2-O- tuned the energy level of L1, so strong dual emission was observed from L1-Eu MOF. In combination with HOMO and LUMO level of L1 and L2, we validated the antenna effect emission. The dual-emission made L1-Eu MOF active as ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visible detection. Importantly, the precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response was revealed. The pore size affected the response through the accessibility of targets as different diffusion dynamics was observed. The targets with big size were blocked directly in the MOFs with small pore. The relative specific surface area affected the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to improve the functionality, to study the response mechanism, and to extend the applications of MOFs.

## Introduction

Metal-Organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous materials prepared with metal nodes and ligands . The porous structure is integrated with functionality of building blocks to improve the applications of MOFs significantly . The pore apertures provide surface and space to realize high adsorption capacity and to differentiate the molecular species with different size . Yaghi et al pioneered that the rigid ligands with different struts, including biphenyl, tetrahydropyrene, pyrene, and terphenyl, were used to realize the controllable pore of MOFs . However, the rigid aromatic ligands are not perfect to extend the pore size due to the large size themselves.

Antenna effect is observed from lanthanide complexes and MOFs . Organic ligand severs as an “antenna” to absorb photons and generates its triplet state (T1) via intersystem crossing (ISC) from singlet state (S1) . The triplet state sensitizes Ln3+ ions to achieve their characteristic emission . Unique luminescent properties are realized, including high quantum yield, large Stokes shift, and bright visible emission . However, the energy level of S1 and T1 is critically limited, so carboxyl benzene is often used to prepare Ln-MOFs with antenna effect emission. Reversely, the π-conjugation structure of polycyclic aromatic ligands decreases the energy level of T1 to forbid energy transfer for the excitation of Ln3+ ions. We have introduced nitrogen atoms into tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)-ethylene to tune the energy level of the ligand, but only the characteristic emission of Eu3+ was excited . Thus, antenna effect and large-pore are seemingly a dilemma for MOFs.

If carboxyl benzenes are connected together through flexible single bond as flexible ligands, the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained, while the size of the ligands are enlarged. Thus, the MOFs with big pore may be prepared, while the energy level of carboxyl benzenes are maintained for antenna effect emission. Flexible ligand is a breakthrough to the traditional opinion that rigid ligands are used to prepare MOFs . As the third generation of porous coordination polymers , flexible MOFs integrate multiple functionality and improve the structure of MOFs to realize dynamic guest inclusion and removal, breathing for reversible response . Thus, flexible MOFs become an important strategy to improve properties and extend applications by taking the advantage of specific structure.

Herein, we developed a flexible ligand to prepare the MOFs with antenna effect and big pore, simultaneously. To this end, trefoil flexible ligand, 1,3,5-tris(5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1) was prepared by attaching three isophthalic acids (L2) to a benzene ring through flexible –CH2-O- group . The flexible Ln-MOF single crystalline was successfully prepared although it is difficult owing to the disorder and the uncertainty of the preparation process . Single crystal result revealed that the aperture is enlarged to 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL for L1-Eu MOF. Moreover, antenna effect emission is observed from L1-Eu and L1-Tb MOFs . The flexible single bond is used to connect isophthalic acid and benzene ring, so L1 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, similar to L2. Moreover, the –CH2-O- group tunes the energy transfer, so L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission at 360 nm and 623 nm under single excitation of 290 nm for ratiometric detection of PO4 3- and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP). Less works studied the effect of porous structure of MOFs on target entrance and linear response range for the analytical purpose. We found small pore of MOFs results in poor linear response because of the different diffusion dynamics of a target at different concentrations. The relative specific surface area affects the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to expand the aperture, improve optical properties, and study the response mechanism for the extensive applications.

## Synthesis of 1,3,5-tris (5-methoxy-1,3-benzene dicarboxylic acid) benzene (L1)

L1 was synthesized according to the previous work . In a typical reaction, a mixture of dimethyl-5-hydroxyisophthalate (2.6 g, 0.0125 mol), KI (23 mg, 0.15 mmol), K2CO3 (6.9 g, 0.05 mol) in DMF (50 mL) was heated to 100 °C for 1 h. 1,3,5-tris (bromomethyl) benzene (0.89 g, 0.0025 mol) was dissolved in DMF (3 mL), added in the above solution drop-wise in 3 min, and heated at 100 °C for 3 h. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and then poured into water to produce a white precipitate. After filtering and washing with ice cold water, the solid was dried in an oven at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 82%). The methyl ester product was dissolved in methanol (40 mL), and an aqueous NaOH solution (2.4 g in 40 mL H2O) was added, 80 °C reflux for 12 h. Then, methanol was evaporated. The solution was acidified to pH 1–2 with HCl (8 M). The precipitate was washed with H2O and dried at 60 °C to obtain a white powder (Yield, 93%).

## Synthesis of L1-Ln MOFs

Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (27 mg, 0.06 mmol) and L1 (13 mg, 0.02 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 2.0 mL), ultrapure water (2.0 mL) and formic acid (HCOOH 0.2 mL). After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 100 °C for 5 days. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the product was washed with water and ethanol to remove the residual L1 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the sample of L1-Eu MOF was obtained. The synthesis of L1-Tb MOF and L1-Gd MOF was similar to that of L1-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Synthesis of L2-Ln MOFs

L2-Eu MOF was synthesized according to the former work . Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (44.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) and L2 (16.6 mg, 0.1 mmol) were dissolved in the mixture of N, N’-dimethylacetamide (DMF 7.0 mL) and ultrapure water (3.0 mL). The as-obtained mixture was transferred to a stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave of 30 mL capacity. After being sonicated for 15 min, the mixture was maintained at 150 °C for 12 h. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the solution was removed by centrifugation and the product was washed with DMF and ethanol to remove the residual L2 and Eu3+ ions, dried at 60 °C overnight. The synthesis of L2-Tb MOF and L2-Gd MOF was similar to that of L2-Eu MOF, only replace Eu(NO3)3·6H2O with Tb(NO3)3·6H2O or Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, respectively.

## Detection of PO4 3- or ATP

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared Na3PO4 solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 70 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm. The fluorescence detection of L2-Eu MOF and L1-Tb MOF for PO4 3- is same as that of the detection of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-. L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF was dispersed in HEPES solution (2 mM, pH = 7.32) to prepare 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF and L2-Eu MOF solution. 0.2 mM freshly prepared ATP solution was added the solution to make the final concentration range from 0 to 50 μM. Their fluorescence spectra were recorded under the excitation of 290 nm.

## Chemical stability test of L1-Eu MOF upon water, acid and base

L1-Eu MOF sample (10 mg for each solvent) was added to different pH aqueous solutions. After immersed for 24 h, the solids were taken out and dried at 60 °C for PXRD data collection.

## Reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3-

L1-Eu MOF was dispersed in PO4 3- (10 μM) to obtain 0.1 mg·mL−1 of L1-Eu MOF solution. After fluorescence detection, the material was washed with ultrapure water and dired at 60 °C. The recycled material was used for fluorescence detection and PXRD data collection. We studied the reusability of L1-Eu MOF for PO4 3- through the process for five times.

## Detection of targets in real samples

The water samples were collected from the Xinkai lake and tap water of Nankai University (Tianjin, China). The lake water was treated with a 0.22 μm filter membrane to remove impurities. A series of water samples containing different concentrations of PO4 3- were prepared by adding different volumes of 0.1 mM PO4 3- standard solution. The fluorescence spectra were tested after the intensity stabilized. Serum samples were selected as a system to detect ATP.

## Structure and energy level of L1

Flexible ligands break the opinion that rigid ligands are used for MOFs. The different modules are connected together through single bonds , so flexible ligands own the properties of the modules and enlarged size, simultaneously. Correspondingly, the functionality of the MOFs is improved significantly. L2 can effectively sensitize Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions, but the pore of L2-Eu MOF is almost completely blocked . Thus, we connected three L2 to benzene ring through –CH2-O- chains to form tri-isophthalate flexible ligand, L1. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and mass spectrometric results confirmed that L1 was successfully prepared . The structure of L1 was illustrated in and expected to retain the optical properties of L2 and expand its size to prepare MOFs with large pore and antenna effect, simultaneously.

Density functional theory (DFT) calculation was first used to reveal the energy level of L1 and L2 . The energy gap between the HOMO and LUMO of L1 is lessened to 4.77 from 5.67 eV of L2. The smaller energy gap results in less energy for electron transition. This was validated with their UV–vis absorption and solid fluorescence. The UV–vis absorption peak of L2 is 280 nm and redshifts to 310 nm for L1 . The solid fluorescence is red-shifted from 360 nm (L2) to 415 nm (L1) . The absorption and fluorescence illustrated that the energy level of L1 is still efficient to sensitize Ln3+ as no big π-conjugation structure forms.

## Preparation and characterization of L1-Ln MOFs

Ln3+ (Eu3+, Tb3+, or Gd3+) and L1 were dissolved in the mixture of DMF/water and then reacted at 100 °C for 5 days with the help of formic acid to prepare L1-Ln MOFs (the detail is listed in SI). Moreover, we obtained the Ln-MOFs single-crystalline . The three MOFs show the same PXRD patterns that agree well with the simulated result, so they show the same structures with high crystallinity ( A). L1-Eu MOF was therefore selected to discuss the structure with single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis results. L1-Eu MOF crystallizes in hexagonal system with the P-62c space group. The asymmetric unit of L1-Eu MOF contains one crystallography independent Eu(III) ions, half of a L1 ligand, half of a bridged oxygen ions of completely deprotonated μ3-O, one dimethylamine cation, and one coordinate water molecules. L1 ligand adopts three distinct coordination modes including bidentate chelate mode, bidentate bridging mode and bidentate 1,3-chelating mode (B). Also, three of nona-coordinated Eu(III) ions share on mutual oxygen center, which further synergizes nine carboxyl groups and three terminal water molecules to construct a tri-core secondary building unit (SBU) (C). The overall framework structure exhibits a three-dimensional (3D) matrix of honeycomb-shape constituted by hexagonal channels with the pore size of ∼18 Å along the c axis (D). It is worth noting that, as far as we know, L1-Eu MOF can be regard as an unprecedented (6, 9)-connected topology net with a point symbol of {411.64}3{430.66}2 which named as nkxyz (Nankai University, Xia, Yin and Zhang) .

L1-Eu MOF exhibits a rod-like structure with the size of ∼3 μm. EDS mapping results reveal the uniform element distribution in the single crystal ( A). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) shows that the frameworks of L1-Ln MOFs are stable until 400 °C. 19.6% of residual solvents are lost at first. The frameworks begin to collapse over 400 °C to leave the oxides with the loss of L1 ligand, demonstrating their high thermal stability (B). Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra of L1 and the MOFs are tested (C). The absorption band of L1 at around 1,710 cm−1 is attributed to the C=O stretching vibration, but a redshift is observed in MOFs. In addition, the broad bands at 2,500–3,000 cm−1 still appears fully in MOFs, so L1 is partly deprotonated to form the MOFs, similar to the single crystal result. The MOFs form through the coordination of –COOH and Ln3+ ions. To evaluate the permanent porosity of L1-Eu MOF, the sample was guest-exchanged with methanol (CH3OH) and activated by supercritical carbon dioxide fluid to yield the guest-free phase. Then, N2 adsorption isotherms were measured. Based on the N2 adsorption data, the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of L1-Eu MOF is 580 m2/g (D) and the pore size is approximately 18 Å (E), which is consistent with the simulated crystal structure . Eu is a heavy atom with high atomic mass, so the big size of L1 ligand plays an important role for the large pore and low density. L2-Eu MOF has also been successfully synthesized. As shown in , the absorption peak of L2 at 1715 cm−1 is attributed to the stretching vibration of C = O, while there is no peak of C = O in L2-Eu MOF, proving the coordination of –COOH and Eu3+, which is consistent with literature reports . As a comparison, the pores of L2-Eu MOF are almost blocked because of the strong steric hindrance with two carboxylic acid groups in the meta position. To verify the robustness of L1-Ln MOFs, the MOFs were immersed in aqueous solutions with pH from 4 to 11. The framework is remained within 24 h at room temperature, illustrating their good chemical stability (A). In addition, L1-Eu MOF was soaked in aqueous solution for 3, 5 and 7 days. B shows that the structure is still intact. Because the strong coordination interaction between carboxyl groups and Ln3+ ions as well as the strong covalent bond in the flexible ligand, the aqueous stability of L1-Eu MOF was therefore confirmed. Thus, L1-Eu MOF shows high stability, high porosity, and low density even flexible ligand is used.

## Antenna effect emission and optical properties of MOFs

The energy level of L1, L2, Eu3+, Tb3+, and Gd3+ ions was recorded to better understand how L1 assembled with three L2 ligands affect the emission behavior of Ln-MOFs . The singlet-state energy (S1) of L1 is 32258 cm−1 (310 nm), while that of L2 is 35714 cm−1 (280 nm). The triplet-state energy (T1) of L1 and L2 is 24813 cm−1 (403 nm) and 22779 cm−1 (439 nm), respectively. The energy gap (ΔE1) between S1 and T1 is 7445 cm−1 and 12935 cm−1 for L1 and L2 . According to Reinhold’s empirical rule, intersystem crossing (ISC) is effective when ΔE1 between S1 and T1 of a ligand is larger than 5000 cm−1. Thus, L1 and L2 can absorb photons to produce its triplet state through ISC efficiently. The antenna effect emission of L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs was then investigated. L1 sensitizes Tb3+ for its efficient antenna effect emission. Similarly, Eu3+ is efficiently excited for its characteristic emission. Interestingly, the emission of L1 is also observed from L1-Eu MOF. The energy gap (ΔE2) between T1 of L1 and the excited state of Eu3+ ions is larger than that of L2, so the incomplete energy transfer occurs for the dual-emission ( A). L2 sensitizes Eu3+ and Tb3+, similar to the previous report (B) . Gd3+ owns higher excited state level and could not be excited by both L1 and L2 (A and 4B). The energy level and transfer between the two ligands and the Ln3+ ions are illustrated in C. L1 maintains the energy level of L2 to excite Eu3+ and Tb3+, while the flexible –CH2-O- group also achieves the strong dual-emission of L1-Eu MOF to facilitate ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visual detection. As a conclusion, the trefoil L1 ligand realizes the large pore size, low density, and the improved efficiency to sensitize both Eu3+ and Tb3+ for their antenna effect emission in the MOFs.

L1-Eu MOF shows dual-emission, so its other optical properties are investigated in detail. The UV–vis absorption spectra of L1 and L1-Eu MOF are recorded (A). A strong absorption peak is observed at 310 nm from L1. However, two absorption peaks are observed at 290 nm and 334 nm from L1-Eu MOF. The peak at 334 nm is attributed to ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT). The emission at 290 nm blue-shifted is due to the twisted structure of L1 in MOFs. The fluorescence spectra of L1-Eu MOF are tested at the excitation wavelengths from 250 to 300 nm with the optimal excitation of 290 nm (B and S12C). The emission from L1 is observed at ∼ 360 nm under the excitation of 290 nm, but the intensity decreases because of the energy transfer to Eu3+ ions (D). Moreover, the strong characteristic emission of Eu3+ ions is observed at 596, 623, 656, and 704 nm from L1-Eu MOF, attributed to the typical f-f transitions of Eu3+ ions, as the transfer of 5D0-7F1, 5D0-7F2, 5D0-7F3, and 5D0-7F4, respectively. Thus, L1 is excited and then sensitizes Eu3+ ions with the antenna effect procedure. In addition, the fluorescence intensity of L1-Eu MOF in pH 3.0–9.0 aqueous system remains stable and the emission of L1-Eu MOF keeps unchanged for at least three days, which is conducive to the detection of targets in different conditions .

## Response of PO4 3- and ATP

Phosphate (PO4 3-) plays an important role in environmental system and biological processes . The high affinity between Ln3+ and PO4 3- has been proved . ATP contains three PO4 3- groups, so it can also interact with L1-Ln MOFs. L1-Ln and L2-Ln MOFs own different pore sizes, so the responses of different MOFs to PO4 3- and ATP were studied to develop the analytical method for PO4 3- and ATP and reveal the effect of pore size and specific area.

The structure of L1-Eu MOF remains unchanged after soaked in Na3PO4 solution for 24 h, revealing that it is extremely stable for PO4 3- detection . As the PO4 3- concentration increases, the emission of L1-Eu MOF at 360 nm enhances, while that at 623 nm decreases slightly ( A). The obvious color change is observed along with the PO4 3- concentration as shown in CIE chromaticity (B). In addition, a linear correlation is observed between the I 360/I 623 ratio and PO4 3- concentration in the range from 1.0 to 45.1 μM with a coefficient of R 2 = 0.987 (C and 5D). A limit of detection (LOD) of 0.183 μM is obtained for PO4 3- and lower than or the same as that of the other fluorescence methods .

As a comparison, the response of L1-Tb MOF to PO4 3- was recorded . Along with the increased PO4 3- content, the emission at 549 nm decreases, while that at 360 nm appears and increases gradually. The decreased emission from Tb ions and the enhanced L1 emission confirmed the antenna effect procedure with the energy transfer from the ligand to Ln3+ ions. The LOD is 7.52 μM and the linear range is 10.1–50.2 μM with the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549. However, the fluorescence change of L1-Tb MOF is indistinguishable for visual detection as illustrated in CIE chromaticity. Thus, L1-Eu MOF provides the possibility for ratiometric sensing and visible detection of PO4 3-. The self-calibration function of the dual-emission improves the sensitivity for PO4 3- with lower LOD than that from L1-Tb MOF.

To explore the selectivity of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3-, the competition experiments were performed for other anions. PO4 3- exhibits the remarkable fluorescence change than other anions ( A and B). The anti-interference capacity was tested with the coexistence of PO4 3- and other anions at four-fold concentration level. The response to PO4 3- is not affected by the interference anions (C and D). The PXRD patterns and fluorescence intensity ratio I 360/I 623 of L1-Eu MOF remain stable after five cycles upon the addition and removal of PO4 3- ions . With the formula of Qt = (C0-Ct)V/m, the adsorption capacity of L1-Eu MOF on PO4 3- was calculated to be 43 mg/g by ion chromatography, which was basically consistent with the result of fluorescence spectroscopy. Thus, L1-Eu MOF is promising for detecting PO4 3- with high selectivity and good recyclability as validated with the analysis of real samples .

The fluorescence response of L1-Eu MOF to ATP was studied. A favorable linearity is observed between the intensity ratio of I 360/I 549 and ATP concentration in the range from 2.0 to 24.9 μM. A low limit of detection (LOD) of ATP was obtained to be 0.147 μM , which owned a superior performance to most sensors for ATP detection . L1-Eu MOF was successfully used for the detection of ATP in real samples . The flexible ligand, L1, achieves the large-pore aperture to insert ATP molecules in the MOF for sensing purpose.

The response of L2-Eu MOF to PO4 3- was further studied as a comparison. The emission at 623 nm decreases slightly with the addition of PO4 3-. A poor linear relationship in the range of 5.0–49.6 μM PO4 3- is obtained with L2-Eu MOF as probe . The decrease in emission at 623 nm is attributed to the interaction of Eu3+ and PO4 3-.

## Response mechanisms

Different response speed and range is observed when MOFs are used as the probes. Similarly, we found different MOFs show different responses to PO4 3- and ATP. High structure stability was observed for L1-Eu MOF in PO4 3- solution. The emission of Eu3+ or Tb3+ decreases, while that from L1 enhances upon the addition of PO4 3-. The result confirmed that PO4 3- or ATP interact to the open sites in the MOFs as the interaction decreases the energy transfer to Eu ions for the increased intensity at 360 nm and the decreased emission at 623 nm. The interaction between Eu3+ and PO4 3- was confirmed with UV–Vis absorption, Infrared, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). As shown in A, after the addition of PO4 3-, the absorption peak of L1-Eu MOF is changed and closed to the absorption of L1. IR shows that the C = O of L1-Eu MOF at 1654 cm−1 blueshifts to 1723 cm−1 after incubation with an aqueous solution of PO4 3- (B). Meanwhile, XPS illustrates the presence of P 2 s after soaked in PO4 3- solution and the slight shift from 529.199 to 529.312 eV of O 1 s is observed ( C, D). In addition, the Eu 3d peaks also display a slight shift from 1132.298 to 1132.394 eV, suggesting the binding of Eu3+ to PO4 3- . Therefore, there is strong interactions between the P-O bonds of PO4 3- and Eu-O cluster. Moreover, as shown in , –COOH of L1 plays an important role in detecting PO4 3- or ATP. and B show that after soaking, the C = O absorption peak of L1 and L1-Eu MOF appear shift. Thus, the response of L1-Eu MOF to PO4 3- and ATP is influenced by the affinity of Eu3+ to phosphate group and the interaction between L1 and phosphate group. With the formula of (F0-F)/F = Kb[Ladd] , we calculated that the binding constants of MOF and PO4 3- or ATP are 4.3 × 104 and 6.3 × 104, respectively. The concentration- and incubation time-dependent responses were then studied to reveal precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response.

L1-Eu MOF shows the same concentration-dependent response for PO4 3- and ATP at low concentration, while ATP exhibits a little high response than PO4 3- at high concentration level ( A). Short incubation time results in the same time-dependent response, but higher response is observed from ATP with long time over PO4 3- (B). The result indicates that not all of three phosphate groups in ATP interact to the open sites. However, almost no fluorescence response was observed to ATP for L2-Eu MOF as the small pore blocks ATP directly (C and 7D). The intensity increases from 0 to 10.0 μM quickly and then becomes slow for PO4 3- with L2-Eu MOF as the probe (C). The pore of L2-Eu MOF is small and blocked for the slow response for PO4 3- ions beyond 10 μM as different diffusion dynamics was observed for the target at different concentrations. ATP molecule was directly blocked because of its big size of ∼ 15 Å. Reversely, L1-Eu MOF owns the pore of 18 Å to allow PO4 3- and ATP entering easily. Thus, the pore size governs the response of the targets because the different diffusion dynamics was observed in L2-Eu MOF for PO4 3- at different concentrations, while ATP was blocked directly.

The mechanism could also be used to explain the linear response range. The linear range of 2.0–24.9 μM is observed for ATP with L1-Eu MOF as probe, narrower than 1.0–45.1 μM for PO4 3-. The same concentration-dependent trend was observed for the two targets (A). Thus, it is not the three phosphate groups that result in the narrow range of ATP, but its big size occupies larger area. The result in C illustrated that the MOFs with small pore exhibited poor linear response of PO4 3- because of the different diffuse dynamics at different concentrations. Thus, the big pore of MOFs improves the accessibility of the targets, while the big relative specific area enlarges the response range. In combination of the dual-emission from antenna effect procedure, the sensing efficiency is obviously improved with L1-Eu MOF as a probe.

## Conclusions

In conclusion, for the first time, we proposed that flexible ligand was used to expand the pore for MOFs and to realize antenna effect, simultaneously. To this end, three –CH2-O- chains were used to connect three L2 ligands to form flexible ligand L1 with a large size. L1 coordinated with Ln3+ ions to form MOFs. Single crystal results indicated that the pore size of L1-Eu MOF was enlarged to ∼ 18 Å with the density of 1.2 g/mL. Moreover, the optical properties of L2 was retained in L1 and flexible –CH2-O- tuned the energy level of L1, so strong dual emission was observed from L1-Eu MOF. In combination with HOMO and LUMO level of L1 and L2, we validated the antenna effect emission. The dual-emission made L1-Eu MOF active as ratiometric fluorescence sensing and visible detection. Importantly, the precise effect of the structure of MOFs on the response was revealed. The pore size affected the response through the accessibility of targets as different diffusion dynamics was observed. The targets with big size were blocked directly in the MOFs with small pore. The relative specific surface area affected the linear response range. Thus, flexible ligand strategy is promising to improve the functionality, to study the response mechanism, and to extend the applications of MOFs.
